title: Self-Active Lipid Nanocapsules Induce GLP‑1 Receptor-Dependent Signaling and Enhance Glucose-Stimulated Insulin Secretion.
abstract: Nanocarriers are typically designed as inert delivery platforms whose biological activity depends on their payloads. Here, we show that blank lipid nanocapsules (LNCs), in the absence of any loaded drug, are intrinsically bioactive and induce glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R)-dependent signaling in pancreatic β-cells. In MIN6 cells and isolated mouse islets, LNCs increased intracellular cAMP (∼2.5- and ∼2.7-fold, respectively) and potentiated glucose-stimulated insulin secretion up to twofold under high glucose, without altering basal secretion. These effects were prevented by the GLP-1R antagonist Exendin-9, the PKA inhibitor H89, and GLP-1R silencing, indicating dependence on GLP-1R receptor signaling. In vivo, intraperitoneal administration of blank LNCs, a route that avoids direct luminal exposure of the intestine and GLP-1 secretion, improved glucose tolerance in healthy and diabetic mice via a GLP-1R-dependent mechanism. The effects of blank LNCs are mimicked by medium-chain fatty acids (caprylic and capric acids), which recapitulated GLP-1R activation and insulinotropic responses. Lipase inhibition abolished both LNCs-induced signaling and functional effects, demonstrating the requirement for triglyceride core processing. Thus, blank LNCs activate GLP-1R signaling in β-cells through an indirect, lipid-mediated mechanism, revealing a previously unrecognized, payload-independent bioactivity of lipid nanocarriers beyond cargo delivery.

title: Primary Mediastinal Kaposiform Hemangioendothelioma Involving the Superior Vena Cava in an Adult: An Extremely Rare Entity.
abstract: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma (KHE) is a rare vascular tumour predominantly affecting infants. Primary mediastinal involvement in adults is exceptionally rare. We report a rare adult case mimicking thymoma but involving the superior vena cava (SVC). A 29-year-old male presented with an anterior mediastinal mass suspected as thymoma. Imaging revealed a solid lesion and the patient underwent surgical resection via median sternotomy. Intraoperatively, the tumour showed dense adherence to the SVC, necessitating SVC plasty. Histopathology confirmed KHE. The patient recovered uneventfully. Although KHE is primarily a paediatric diagnosis, it must be considered in the differential diagnosis of adult anterior mediastinal masses. Complete surgical resection remains the treatment of choice, though vascular reconstruction may be required due to the tumour's infiltrative nature.
summary_short: We report a rare adult case mimicking thymoma but involving the superior vena cava (SVC).

title: Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon revealed by a rehabilitation referral for upper-limb heaviness in an adult with a giant hepatic haemangioma: a case report.
abstract: Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon (KMP) is a consumptive coagulopathy arising within a vascular tumour. It is exceptional in adults, where a giant hepatic haemangioma is the usual substrate. We report a 42-year-old woman referred for physical and rehabilitation medicine assessment of a 3-day heaviness of the left upper limb; brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) obtained for a suspected stroke was normal. The disability contrasted with a normal neurological examination, while complete physical examination found tenderness over the liver. A blood count showed haemoglobin at 7 g/dl with reticulocytosis and platelets falling from 25 to 6 × 10 9 /l. Ultrasound, computed tomography, and MRI showed a 112 × 100 mm centrally liquefied hepatic mass with progressive centripetal enhancement, indicating a bleeding giant haemangioma with KMP. Emergency transarterial embolization was decided, but the patient died in the angiography suite from fulminant haemorrhagic shock. A functional limb complaint may be the only visible sign of a lethal consumptive coagulopathy.

title: Disruption of FOS/JUN dimerization synergizes with mTOR inhibition in pancreatic cancer.
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a lethal malignancy where systemic chemotherapy remains the standard of care. Here, we demonstrate that BMVC-8C3O, initially characterized as a G-quadruplex stabilizer, exhibits preferential toxicity toward PDAC cells due to greater cellular uptake relative to non-cancerous cells. Combining BMVC-8C3O with mTOR inhibitors (Torin-1 or rapamycin) induced synergistic cytotoxicity in PDAC cells. Functional rescue experiments identified FOS as the pivotal determinant of this synergy, as ectopic FOS expression abolished the therapeutic benefit, underscoring the necessity of simultaneously blocking mTOR and FOS pathways to achieve synthetic lethality. Mechanistically, BMVC-8C3O disrupts FOS/JUN heterodimerization and reduces FOS protein stability and abundance, thereby impairing AP-1-mediated transcriptional activity and functionally redefining this compound as a targeted FOS inhibitor in PDAC. In vivo, BMVC-8C3O combined with Torin-1 effectively suppressed tumor growth in MIA PaCa-2 xenografts without systemic toxicity. Collectively, our findings establish a compelling rationale for concurrent mTOR and FOS inhibition as a potent therapeutic strategy for PDAC.
summary_short: Here, we demonstrate that BMVC-8C3O, initially characterized as a G-quadruplex stabilizer, exhibits preferential toxicity toward PDAC cells due to greater cellular uptake relative to non-cancerous cells.

title: SATAY-based chemogenomic screening uncovers antifungal resistance mechanisms and key determinants of ATI-2307 and chitosan sensitivity.
abstract: Multidrug-resistant fungal pathogens are a serious threat to public health and global food security. Mitigation requires the discovery of antifungal compounds with novel modes of action along with a comprehensive understanding of the molecular mechanisms governing antifungal resistance. Here, we apply saturated transposon analysis in yeast (SATAY), a powerful transposon sequencing method in Saccharomyces cerevisiae , to uncover loss- and gain-of-function mutations conferring resistance to 20 different antifungal compounds. These screens identify a diverse array of novel resistance mechanisms and multiple modes of action. SATAY is performed in drug-sensitive strains to generate chemogenomic profiles for compounds that lack activity against conventional laboratory strains. This study therefore provides a significant resource for exploring cellular responses to chemical stresses. We discover that the natural antifungal chitosan electrostatically interacts with cell wall mannosylphosphate and that the transporter Hol1 concentrates the novel antifungal ATI-2307 within yeast. This latter finding presents an avenue for drug design initiatives but also unveils a straightforward evolutionary path to ATI-2307 resistance with minimal fitness cost.
summary_short: Multidrug-resistant fungal pathogens are a serious threat to public health and global food security. Mitigation requires the discovery of antifungal compounds with novel modes of action along with a comprehensive understanding of the molecular mechanisms governing antifungal resistance.

title: Mechanism of the lysosomal calcium signaling TRPML1-TFEB axis in Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a prevalent chronic neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive apoptosis of midbrain substantia nigra dopaminergic neurons, striatal dopamine depletion, and α-synuclein (α-syn)-positive Lewy-body formation. Patients exhibit motor deficits (resting tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia, postural instability) plus non-motor manifestations such as cognitive and sleep impairment. PD pathogenesis arises from intertwined mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, defective protein degradation and disrupted calcium homeostasis, whose precise mechanisms remain incompletely defined. As both a degradative organelle and signaling hub, lysosomes govern clearance of proteins and damaged organelles and mediate key neuronal events through calcium-dependent signaling. Transient Receptor Potential Mucolipin 1 (TRPML1), a lysosomal calcium-release channel, and Transcription Factor EB (TFEB), a master regulator of lysosome biogenesis and autophagic flux, constitute the conserved TRPML1-TFEB axis that couples lysosomal calcium signaling to transcriptional control of cellular degradation. title: Targeting PI3K signalling for broad inhibition of β-Coronavirus infection.
abstract: The phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) signalling pathway plays a central role in regulating key cellular processes such as survival, metabolism, and immune responses. Aberrant activation of this pathway is associated with tumorigenesis, and several PI3K inhibitors have been developed as anticancer agents. Emerging evidence suggests that viruses, including β-coronaviruses, have evolved mechanisms to exploit host PI3K signalling for their replication and immune evasion. In this study, we evaluated the antiviral efficacy of a panel of PI3K inhibitors against β-coronaviruses, including murine hepatitis virus (MHV), human OC43 (HuCoV-OC43) and four major SARS-CoV-2 variants using both cell line and organoid models. Our findings reveal that these compounds exhibit low micromolar potency in inhibiting viral replication. Notably, the PI3K/mTOR inhibitor C20 (PWT33597) demonstrated broad-spectrum activity against multiple β-coronaviruses, including SARS-CoV-2, MHV, and HuCoV-OC43, in conventional cell lines and in air-liquid interface (ALI)-cultured, differentiated primary human bronchial epithelial cells. Given that cytokine storm is a major contributor to SARS-CoV-2-related multi-organ failure and mortality, we further explored the impact of PI3K inhibition on host inflammatory responses. title: When Interleukin-1 Blockade Is Not Equal: Differential Response to Anakinra and Canakinumab in NLRP1-Associated Autoinflammation.
abstract: Introduction NLRP1-associated autoinflammation with arthritis and dyskeratosis (NAIAD) is a rare inflammasomopathy characterised by excessive interleukin-1 (IL-1) signalling, systemic inflammation, arthritis, dyskeratotic skin lesions, and growth impairment. Experience with targeted biologic therapy remains limited. Method We describe a child with genetically confirmed NAIAD who demonstrated differential responses to IL-1-targeted therapies. Results A 9-year-old boy with a de novo pathogenic NLRP1 variant presented with severe immune dysregulation characterised by recurrent fevers, inflammatory arthritis, hepatosplenomegaly, dyskeratotic skin disease, inflammatory keratitis, growth failure, and persistently elevated inflammatory markers. Initial treatment with sirolimus was limited by pancytopenia and inadequate disease control. High-dose anakinra (>6 mg/kg/day) resulted in partial clinical improvement, particularly of arthritis and systemic inflammation; however, serum amyloid A remained elevated and significant disease manifestations persisted. To improve disease control, adjunctive baricitinib was introduced but was subsequently ceased following worsening cytopenias and a significant primary Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection requiring hospitalisation. Given ongoing inflammation and concerns regarding long-term risk of amyloidosis, canakinumab was approved and commenced at 4 mg/kg every four weeks. summary_short: Introduction NLRP1-associated autoinflammation with arthritis and dyskeratosis (NAIAD) is a rare inflammasomopathy characterised by excessive interleukin-1 (IL-1) signalling, systemic inflammation, arthritis, dyskeratotic skin lesions, and growth impairment. Experience with targeted biologic therapy remains limited.

title: Better Late than Never? Allogeneic Stem Cell Transplantation for Chronic Granulomatous Disease in Early Adulthood.
abstract: Introduction Chronic granulomatous disease (CGD) is an inherited disorder of phagocyte function caused by defective NADPH oxidase activity, resulting in recurrent infection and dysregulated granulomatous inflammation. Although allogeneic stem cell transplantation (alloSCT) is increasingly performed early as definitive therapy, older patients with longstanding CGD present unique challenges due to cumulative infectious and inflammatory complications. Case presentation We report the case of a 17-year-old patient with CGD diagnosed in South Korea at two months of age who presented to Christchurch Hospital with disseminated aspergillosis with pulmonary and osseous involvement. His disease course prior to this was complicated by recurrent pneumonia, granulomatous osteomyelitis, necrotic lymphadenopathy, colitis, and extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) Klebsiella pneumoniae infection. Given his significant infectious burden, his case was discussed through Transplantation and Primary Immunodeficiency (TAPID) networks, where international expert opinion suggested he may have been beyond the optimal window and high risk for alloSCT, with initial recommendations to explore emerging gene therapy trials. Following review with the National Institutes of Health (NIH), Bethesda, he underwent matched unrelated donor peripheral blood alloSCT through a clinical trial (D0 = December 20, 2024). title: Comparison of anti-hyperuricemic activity of berberine and metformin: Insight from de novo purine biosynthesis and purine metabolism and intestinal microbiome.
abstract: Increasing evidence has shown that the worldwide epidemic of metabolic disease including hyperuricemia (HUA) correlates with an elevation in serum uric acid (UA) as well as a marked increase in total fructose intake. Phellodendri Chinensis Cortex (PC) is a traditional medicinal material used to treat metabolic diseases including gout and HUA. Berberine (BBR), the main component of PC, possesses anti-HUA and anti-gout effects. Metformin is widely used for the treatment of metabolic syndrome. However, their effect on HUA induced by high-fructose remained unexplored. The present work endeavored to explore the anti-HUA potential of BBR and metformin on high-fructose-induced hyperuricemic rats focusing on intestinal microbiota, de novo purine biosynthesis (DNPB) of endogenous purine, purine cycle and metabolism and intestinal microbiota. Results indicated that BBR and metformin remarkably decreased the high levels of UA, creatinine, and urea induced by a long-term high-fructose diet. BBR and metformin activated the expression of ketohexokinase (KHK) and suppressed the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) to regulate fructose metabolism. Following that, BBR and metformin suppressed the activated DNPB induced by high-fructose, through which a great number of purine synthesis was inhibited. Besides, BBR promoted the purine salvage pathway (PSP) and suppressed the expression of xanthine oxidase (XOD) to inhibit the purine metabolism, resulting in the increase of inosine and decrease of IMP

title: Nonsurgical management of Chiari malformation type I and syringomyelia and the potential role of inflammation in the pathophysiology of Chiari-associated syrinx: illustrative cases.
abstract: Background Chiari malformation type I (CM-I) is characterized by cerebellar tonsil position ≥ 5 mm below the foramen magnum, which can disrupt CSF flow and lead to syringomyelia. Pro-inflammatory processes have been associated with heightened CNS inflammation and altered CSF dynamics, mechanisms that may contribute to CM-I and syringomyelia pathogenesis, although the precise relationship remains uncertain. Anti-inflammatory interventions, including dietary modification and pharmacological therapies such as metformin, may offer neuroprotective benefits by mitigating neuroinflammation and improving neurological outcomes. Observations The authors describe the cases of 2 pediatric patients with CM-I and syringomyelia who demonstrated clinical and radiographic improvement following anti-inflammatory interventions. Both patients initially presented with symptomatic CM-I, cerebellar tonsil position > 5 mm below the foramen magnum, and syringomyelia. A 7-year-old female was started on a diet intended to reduce inflammation and restrict gluten and sugar and subsequently demonstrated stable tonsil position, reduced syrinx size, and symptomatic improvement of hand paresthesias. A 9-year-old female began metformin therapy and experienced stable tonsil position, reduction in a multiloculated syrinx, and resolution of symptoms. Lessons These cases suggest that anti-inflammatory interventions may contribute to symptom improvement and syrinx reduction in CM-I-associated syringomyelia, suppor

title: Placental growth factor in early pregnancy: Gestational week-specific reference intervals and influence of maternal factors across three automated immunoassays in a Swedish cohort.
abstract: Introduction Placental growth factor (PlGF) is an established biomarker for first-trimester preeclampsia prediction. However, concentrations vary between assay platforms due to calibration and methodological differences. Gestational age-specific PlGF reference intervals are limited. We aimed to derive gestational week-specific PlGF reference intervals across three platforms and to assess factors associated with PlGF concentrations in a Swedish population. Material and methods This descriptive cross-sectional study used data from the Swedish IMPACT cohort. Blood samples collected at 11 + 0 to 14 + 6 weeks were analyzed for PlGF on Revvity, Roche Diagnostics, and Thermo Fisher Scientific platforms. A reference subgroup of uncomplicated singleton pregnancies was used to derive gestational week-specific reference intervals. Associations between maternal and pregnancy-related factors and PlGF were examined in the full study population using log-linear regression. Variable importance was assessed using Shapley values. Results Of 12 908 IMPACT participants, 12 099 had a valid PlGF measurement and were included in the study population. The healthy reference subgroup comprised 7719 participants. In this subgroup, PlGF concentrations rose 23% per week across platforms. At 11 + 0 to 11 + 6 weeks, reference intervals (2.5th-97.5th percentiles) were 6.0-50.8 ng/L for Revvity, 16.4-67.7 ng/L for Roche, and 10.0-51.0 ng/L for Thermo Fisher. At 12 + 0 to 12 + 6 weeks, intervals were 8.9-69.5
summary_short: We aimed to derive gestational week-specific PlGF reference intervals across three platforms and to assess factors associated with PlGF concentrations in a Swedish population.

title: Engineered exosomes: a revolutionary tool for precision medicine and disease treatment.
abstract: Engineered exosomes have been recognized as promising natural delivery vehicles for precision medicine by virtue of their excellent biocompatibility, inherent ability to penetrate various biological barriers and remarkable potential for functional modification. However, current research remains predominantly preclinical, with unresolved product heterogeneity, variable intracellular cargo release, and limited evidence linking engineering choices to patient-specific benefit. The present review first summarizes the core biological properties of extracellular vesicles and focuses on the unique characteristics of exosomes in terms of classification, biogenesis, molecular structure and physiological functions. Then, our review systematically organizes three major categories of exosome engineering technologies including donor cell selection, diverse cargo loading modes and multiple surface functionalization strategies, and objectively analyzes the practical advantages and existing translational limitations of each technique. It also summarizes the latest research progress of engineered exosomes applied in multiple fields such as oncology, neurodegenerative diseases, tissue regeneration, gene therapy and inflammatory disorders. This work further discusses key challenges including exosomal heterogeneity, unstable intracellular cargo release, large-scale manufacturing difficulties and imperfect regulatory standards that severely restrict clinical transformation. title: Chimeric antigen receptor-engineered ILC2s for targeted immune regulation.
abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) engineering has transformed cellular immunotherapies, yet whether CAR signaling can direct innate lymphoid cell functions for therapeutic applications has not been established. IL-10-producing ILC2s (ILC2 10 ) suppress pathogenic T cell responses in preclinical transplant models, making them attractive candidates for engineered regulatory cell therapies. Here we show that CD28 and CD3z are endogenous signaling modules with distinct expression kinetics in ILC2 activation. We engineered human ILC2 10 with CARs incorporating these domains and demonstrate that CAR activation via CD3z, CD28 or both induces robust proliferation and cytokine production, with each domain inducing distinct transcriptional programs, and combined CD3z and CD28 signaling uniquely inducing cytotoxic programs. In a xenogeneic graft-versus-host disease model, CAR-ILC2 10 more effectively inhibited human T cell engraftment and activity, displayed enhanced persistence and trafficked to sites of T cell-mediated injury. These findings establish CAR-ILC2s as programmable cellular therapies, with CAR signaling architecture shaping distinct ILC2 effector programs.

title: Antimicrobial peptides are differentially regulated in blood and visceral adipose tissue in obesity-associated metabolic dysfunction and linked to NLRP3-related signaling.
abstract: Obesity is characterized by chronic low-grade inflammation in which visceral adipose tissue (VAT) plays a central immunometabolic role. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) integrate host defense and inflammatory signaling, but their regulation across metabolic compartments in human obesity remains incompletely defined. We evaluated circulating AMP concentrations and gene expression levels in VAT and circulating leukocytes from 108 participants classified according to obesity and glycemic status. These analyses were complemented with mechanistic studies in human visceral adipocytes evaluating inflammatory and microbiota-related stimuli, effects of NLR family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3)related modulation, and crosstalk with PMA-differentiated THP-1 macrophage-like cells. Obesity was associated with a selective circulating AMP profile characterized by higher cathelicidin, calprotectin, lipocalin-2 and neutrophil elastase together with lower α-defensin 6 and β-defensin 1. In VAT, obesity was accompanied by increased expression of several inflammatory AMP-related genes together with higher NLRP3 and NLRP6 expression and reduced DEFB1, with additional differences emerging across glycemic groups. Circulating leukocytes displayed a partially overlapping but distinct transcriptional profile, consistent with compartment-specific regulation rather than a generalized AMP response. title: Beyond chronological age: physical function and muscle health as clinically meaningful ageing clocks.
Active living for healthy ageing: time for multilevel action.
Physical exercise interventions to promote healthy ageing in older adults: from research to clinical implementation.
abstract: Physical exercise interventions have emerged as a key strategy to promote healthy ageing; however, they remain insufficiently implemented in real-world contexts. In this Series paper, we synthesised the current evidence on the effects of exercise interventions on functional ability and intrinsic capacity-the marker of healthy ageing defined by WHO that encompasses all the individual's mental and physical capacities-among older adults (aged ≥60 years) across diverse settings. The most effective exercise prescription strategies, and ongoing research gaps and implementation barriers, are also discussed. Evidence consistently supports multicomponent exercise programmes, including strength, aerobic, and balance training, as effective strategies to preserve or restore intrinsic capacity and overall functional ability in older adults, ranging from community-dwelling individuals to hospitalised individuals, individuals with frailty, or long-term care residents. Although the most pronounced benefits on intrinsic capacity are observed within the locomotion domain, improvements also extend to the cognitive, psychological, and vitality domains, particularly when exercise is part of a larger multidomain lifestyle intervention (eg, incorporating cognitive training or dietary interventions). In summary, exercise is a cornerstone intervention for healthy ageing, being effective across different levels of functional capacity and care settings. title: Building the future for active ageing: a scoping meta-review of progress and prospects for physical activity promotion in later life.
abstract: Regular physical activity is among the most beneficial health-related investments people can make, particularly as they age. However, many older adults (aged 45 years and older) worldwide remain insufficiently active to obtain its many related benefits. This Series paper reviews current strategies and identifies research gaps and future directions for physical activity interventions that are effective and potentially resource efficient. Using a socioecological framework, we conducted a scoping meta-review of reviews on older adults published between 2010 and 2025 in the PubMed, PsycINFO, Embase, and CINAHL databases, with 12 reviews considered as relevant and supplemented with 80 other relevant articles based on the areas identified. The Series paper describes effective physical activity interventions and highlights emerging directions for intervention at the micro, meso, and macro socioecological levels. From this synthesis, we describe 11 priority directions for physical activity interventions, including embedding participatory approaches in strengthening the strategies for long-term physical activity maintenance and implementation; embedding climate-related considerations into programme design for older adults; expanding investigations of under-researched yet promising intervention formats, content areas, and delivery contexts; leveraging technology to enhance intervention reach and older adult participation and inclusion; ensuring that environmental and policy interventio
summary_short: Regular physical activity is among the most beneficial health-related investments people can make, particularly as they age. However, many older adults (aged 45 years and older) worldwide remain insufficiently active to obtain its many related benefits.

title: Physical activity, sedentary behaviour, and healthy ageing in older adults.
abstract: Physical activity and sedentary behaviour are key modifiable determinants of physical, cognitive, and psychosocial function that collectively shape the ageing process. Despite these known benefits, the global rates of insufficient physical activity and sedentary behaviour have dramatically increased, particularly among adults older than 60 years. The 2020 WHO physical activity and sedentary behaviour guidelines for older adults were primarily informed by self-reported observational research. Therefore, these guidelines are prone to recall and social desirability biases and often fail to capture the complexity of physical activity and sedentary behaviour patterns, such as volume, intensity, and bout duration. As research using wearable devices increases, our understanding of how these physical activity and sedentary behaviour patterns relate to prospective health outcomes expands. In this Series paper, we provide an overview of the current evidence on how physical activity and sedentary behaviour patterns are associated with health outcomes in older adults, with a focus on wearable-based evidence. We highlight the benefits of light, moderate, and vigorous physical activity, and their joint associations with sedentary behaviour. Growing prospective evidence supports the importance of incidental physical activity accumulated through normal daily living, even when accrued through brief, intermittent bursts, which might be more behaviourally sustainable for older adults. Beyond Fertility: Pioneering AI-Enhanced Health Solutions with AMH and Inhibin B.
abstract: The review article underscores the pivotal roles of Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH) and Inhibin B in the realm of reproductive health. AMH, with its stable secretion patterns irrespective of the menstrual cycle, serves as a robust indicator of the quantity of remaining oocytes, offering a reliable measure for ovarian reserve, predicting ovarian longevity and fertility potential. This makes AMH an indispensable tool in both fertility assessments for women contemplating delayed childbearing and in evaluating the risk of conditions like premature ovarian insufficiency. On the other hand, Inhibin B provides critical insights into ovarian function. Its levels peak during the early follicular phase and are closely tied to the growth of the dominant follicle, regulated by and in turn regulating Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH). This interplay offers a dynamic view of the real-time ovarian response, thus contributing to the chances of successful outcomes. The integration of these biomarkers and other common clinical indicators into AI-driven diagnostic tools marks a significant advancement in personalized medicine. Such tools leverage complex algorithms to analyze biomarker levels and predict individual reproductive outcomes with greater accuracy. The future of these biomarkers in clinical practice looks promising, with ongoing research aimed at refining their predictive power and expanding their application. title: Exercise Reprograms the Epigenetic-Mitochondrial Axis: Mechanisms of Healthy Aging across Muscle, Brain, and Heart.
abstract: Aging manifests as a progressive, multi-hallmark deterioration involving epigenetic dysregulation, mitochondrial impairment, proteostatic collapse, and persistent inflammaging. Accumulating evidence positions habitual physical exercise as one of the most effective non-pharmacological geroprotectors, capable of inducing beneficial, partially reversible epigenetic reprogramming across multiple tissues. This comprehensive review synthesizes current understanding of how different exercise modalitiesendurance, resistance, and high-intensity interval trainingelicit targeted changes in DNA methylation, histone posttranslational modifications, and microRNA (miRNA) networks, collectively restoring mitochondrial biogenesis, dynamics, mitophagy, and redox homeostasis in aging skeletal muscle, brain, and heart. Special emphasis is placed on the dual role of reactive oxygen species (ROS): physiological, exercise-induced ROS pulses function as pivotal redox signals that interface with AMPK-SIRT1-PGC-1α signaling, TET-mediated demethylation, Class IIa HDAC nuclear export, and miRNA maturation, thereby driving adaptive mitochondrial and proteostatic responses rather than oxidative damage. Circulating exerkines and myokines (irisin, IL-6, BDNF, apelin) further orchestrate interorgan communication, linking muscle-derived signals to hippocampal neuroplasticity and cardiac metabolic resilience. Sex-specific epigenetic patterns and differential responsiveness to exercise intensity are highlighted

title: Mitochondrial-Wide Association Studies: Integrating Population-Based Data and Mitochondrial Genetics.
abstract: Mitochondrial-wide association studies (MiWAS) extend genome-wide association frameworks to systematically test mitochondrial DNA variants for their associations with aging-related phenotypes. Unlike nuclear DNA, the mitochondrial genome is maternally inherited, lacks recombination, and encodes core components of oxidative phosphorylation, making it central to energy metabolism and cellular stress responses. This chapter provides a comprehensive protocol for conducting MiWAS using population-based aging cohorts, with a focus on practical implementation using publicly available datasets such as the Health and Retirement Study. We describe essential steps, including obtaining institutional approvals and data access, preparing phenotype files with appropriate covariates, extracting mitochondrial variants from genotype arrays, performing ethnic-stratified association testing, and interpreting results with multiple testing corrections. Key considerations include accounting for population stratification through mitochondrial genetic ancestry, selecting appropriate minor allele frequency thresholds, and validating findings through sensitivity analyses and replication. By making methods to assess mitochondrial genetic variation, such as MiWAS, accessible to aging researchers, this opens new opportunities to identify genetic determinants of longevity, age-related disease risk, and mitochondrial-nuclear interactions that shape healthy aging.
summary_short: Mitochondrial-wide association studies (MiWAS) extend genome-wide association frameworks to systematically test mitochondrial DNA variants for their associations with aging-related phenotypes. title: Practical Guide to RNA Sequencing Analysis in Aging Research.
abstract: Aging is accompanied by widespread changes in gene expression, which underlie functional and structural declines in organisms over time. Transcriptome analysis, including RNA sequencing, has become an essential approach in modern research on biological processes, including aging, but remains challenging for many experimental scientists. Here, we provide a practical protocol for RNA sequencing analysis for aging research.

title: Practical Considerations for Automated Lifespan Measures in C. elegans.
abstract: Many strengths of C. elegans as a model organism make them amenable for aging studies, including a short lifespan, the ability to produce a large number of isogenic progeny, and the availability of genetic tools, including genome-wide RNA interference (RNAi) libraries and robust gene-editing strategies. These strengths are complemented by the ability to perform high-throughput lifespan measurements, including automated strategies. Given the development of several systems to automate the measurement of lifespans, deciding between these options can depend on several factors, such as pricing, customizability, throughput, troubleshooting, and more. We provide a discussion of considerations for several methods and provide detailed protocols for implementing a scanner-based lifespan machine system with minor modifications to the existing version.

title: Isolation and Functional Screening of Plant-Derived Natural Products for Assessing Healthy Aging and Neuroprotective Activities in Caenorhabditis elegans.
abstract: Plant-derived natural products are a rich source of bioactive molecules with potential benefits for healthy aging and neuroprotection. Identifying compounds with these activities requires integrated platforms capable of evaluating multiple aspects of organismal health. Caenorhabditis elegans provides a genetically tractable, physiologically conserved in vivo model ideally suited for functional screening of natural products. This protocol presents a comprehensive workflow for preparing plant extracts, characterizing their antioxidant properties, and assessing their effects on stress resistance, healthspan, lifespan, and neuroprotective effects in C. elegans. Methods begin with plant extraction and routine maintenance of nematode and bacterial cultures to ensure consistency across experiments. Antioxidant activity is assessed through oxidative stress resistance assays, intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) quantification, stress-responsive reporter activation, and subcellular localization of the transcription factors DAF-16/FOXO and SKN-1/Nrf2. Healthspan assessments include lipofuscin accumulation, pharyngeal pumping, reproductive function, growth, and locomotion. Longevity effects are determined using lifespan assays. Neuroprotective potential is examined in models of β-amyloid/tau toxicity, chemotaxis impairment, polyglutamine aggregation, and α-synuclein aggregation relevant to Alzheimer's, Huntington's, and Parkinson's diseases. summary_short: Plant-derived natural products are a rich source of bioactive molecules with potential benefits for healthy aging and neuroprotection. Identifying compounds with these activities requires integrated platforms capable of evaluating multiple aspects of organismal health.

title: Calculating Epigenetic Clocks from DNA Methylation Data to Index Accelerated Epigenetic Aging.
abstract: Reliable biomarkers to assess biological age are important in geroscience research. Reliable estimators of biological aging have been quantified from epigenetic data, specifically DNA methylation, a modification of DNA that does not change the sequence but can impact gene regulation. DNA methylation patterns quantified into summary markers of epigenetic aging that use years of age as their metric are called epigenetic clocks because they represent the ticking of biological time. As more DNA methylation data become available through large population-based studies, biobanks, and clinical studies, there is a growing need to document methodological protocols for calculating epigenetic clocks for all researchers, including those who do not typically work in the epigenetic space. Some of the most widely used clocks in geroscience research include Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, and GrimAge. This chapter provides a step-by-step guide for researchers new to DNA methylation analysis and introduces the principles of epigenetic clock calculation methods in the R programming language. This protocol provides guidance for calculating the clocks in addition to elucidating the necessary steps for quality control analysis of human DNA methylation data.
summary_short: Reliable biomarkers to assess biological age are important in geroscience research. Reliable estimators of biological aging have been quantified from epigenetic data, specifically DNA methylation, a modification of DNA that does not change the sequence but can impact gene regulation.

title: Multilevel Factors Associated With On-Site Childcare Availability in Substance Use Disorder Treatment Settings, United States, 2024.
abstract: Background Most parents in need of substance use disorder (SUD) treatment do not receive it, due in part to childcare being a major barrier. Childcare availability likely depends on multiple factors at the facility, community, and state policy levels. Objective To identify multilevel characteristics associated with childcare availability in SUD treatment settings, and whether state policies about drug use and treatment influenced childcare availability differently within states. Methods We used the Mental Health and Addiction Treatment Tracking Repository (MATTR) and external geocoded data to identify all known licensed SUD outpatient treatment facilities in the United States (2024; N = 7796). We used multilevel logistic regression to model childcare availability. We included interactions to test whether state policies about drug use and childcare were associated with childcare access differently depending on census tract characteristics. Results Only 4% of SUD treatment facilities offered childcare (n = 323). Location in a state that did not specifically mention methamphetamine in its child endangerment laws was most strongly associated with childcare access in communities with higher Black population density ( = -0.16, standard error = 0.06, P = .01). Conclusion Some state policies influenced childcare access differently in different communities, suggesting that state policies should be flexible and tailored to the needs of diverse localities.

title: Population-Level Awareness of Water Safety Messages: An Analysis of a Representative Sample From New South Wales, Australia.
abstract: Issue addressed The World Health Organisation recommends strengthening public awareness of drowning through strategic communications as a key drowning prevention strategy. This study aimed, for the first time, to assess population-level awareness of water safety messages in New South Wales, Australia. Methods Via an age-sex representative sample survey, community beliefs around the number of water safety messages and awareness of messages (defined as having seen or heard) were examined. Message awareness variance between different demographics (gender, age group, country of birth, rurality and socio-economic classification of residence) and water use frequency groups was assessed using chi square tests. Results The sample comprised 1495 people (52% female; 33% 45-64 years; 84% Australian-born and 78% metropolitan residents). Seventy-six percent did not believe the number of water safety messages promoted to the community was confusing. 'Swim between the flags' had the highest awareness among the sample (68%), followed by 'No flags, no swim' (53%). Despite no longer being actively promoted, 36% were aware of the message 'To escape a rip, swim parallel to the beach'. 'Respect the River' had significantly higher awareness among males, Australian-born and regional residents, at-risk cohorts for river drowning. Conclusions Message longevity supports increased awareness, though awareness varies by message and demographic groups. Funding support to increase awareness should reflect

title: Isolation of Keratinocytes from Human Hair Follicles and Selection of a Population Enriched in Epithelial Stem and Progenitor Cells by Flow Cytometry.
abstract: The human hair follicle (HF) harbors distinct populations of epithelial stem and progenitor cells that are essential for hair homeostasis and epidermal wound healing. While the follicular niche, the anatomical equivalent of the murine bulge located at the insertion site of the arrector pili muscle, has historically been the primary target for the isolation of hair follicle stem cells (HFSCs), capturing the full epithelial stem and progenitor hierarchy within the outer root sheath (ORS) is critical for a comprehensive understanding of human hair follicle biology. As integrin α6 (CD49f) is a well-established surface marker associated with basal epithelial stem and progenitor states, and long-term proliferative potential of immature keratinocytes, we have exploited this marker to isolate an epithelial cell population corresponding to the keratinocyte basal layer of the ORS. This chapter describes a protocol for the enrichment of stem and progenitor cells from intact human hair follicles, combining manual microdissection of the entire hair follicle, enzymatic dissociation, and flow cytometry sorting based on CD49f expression.Functional validation using in vitro proliferation and clone-forming assays showed that the CD49f high fraction exhibits significantly greater proliferative and clonogenic capacity, compared to the ORS total and CD49f low populations. title: Predicting Gastrointestinal Complications After Cardiac Surgery From Mean Arterial Blood Pressure Under a Data-Driven Threshold for Hypotension: Protocol for an Advanced Database Study.
abstract: Background Hypotension during cardiopulmonary bypass may increase the risk of gastrointestinal complications due to insufficient splanchnic autoregulatory capacity. We hypothesize that both duration and level of blood pressure below a data-driven threshold during cardiopulmonary bypass are associated with the risk of gastrointestinal complications. Methods Patients who underwent cardiac surgery at Copenhagen University Hospital, Rigshospitalet, during 2018-2022 will be included if they underwent on-pump valve surgery, coronary artery bypass grafting, and/or surgery on the ascending aorta. The primary outcome is major gastrointestinal complications within 30 days, defined as acute intestinal ischemia, abdominal surgery, bowel perforation, or gastrointestinal hemorrhage. Secondary endpoints are serious gastrointestinal complications, delayed recovery of bowel function, cholinesterase inhibitor administration, and 30-day mortality. The exposure is the exposure to lower blood pressure, calculated as the product of the duration and level of blood pressure below a data-driven threshold. To identify the optimal threshold, we split the population in a training (75%) and validation cohort (25%). In the training cohort we will identify the threshold with the highest area under the receiver operating curve for the primary outcome. title: [Healthy longevity strategies in developed countries: overview of national approaches].
abstract: The concept of healthy longevity, which means an increase in the duration of a healthy, active life, and not just its duration, is becoming key to shaping policy on aging in developed countries. This review examines how individual high-income countries have conceptualized and implemented the principles of healthy longevity. The analysis shows a broad alignment of national strategies with the resolution of the United Nations Decade for Healthy Aging (2021-2030), however, significant differences in approaches to implementation are revealed. The United States focuses on ten-year goals for public health and community-based system transformation. Singapore has transformed its leisure centers into comprehensive medical and social centers. Spain demonstrates a high degree of convergence of regional approaches with the UN framework programmes, while the UK has set ambitious but difficult-to-achieve goals to increase healthy life expectancy by five years by 2035. Australia's approach is unique in that it is shaped by the integration of climate and health issues, as well as the need to reform the care system for the elderly. In all the countries reviewed, the concept of healthy longevity encompasses prevention, interagency coordination, reduction of health inequalities, and transformation of increased life expectancy into years of functional independence and high quality of life.

title: [THE SOCIOLOGICAL ASPECTS OF OCCUPATIONAL MEDICINE: TO PROBLEM STATEMENT (THE REVIEW)].
abstract: The purpose of the study is to summarize and to analyze results of national and foreign studies concerning incorporation of sociological studies in occupational medicine. The analysis of databases of PubMed, eLibrary, Cohrane Library, MEDLINE was carried out according keywords: sociology of occupational medicine, social factors, occupational risk, occupational diseases, occupational pathology, the occupational risk management system. The sampling for analysis included 257 sources. The publications review permitted to substantiate incorporation of sociological studies on medicine, health, traumatism, morbidity, labor, employment, professions and risk as basis for new problem field in occupational medicine. This area can be denoted as the sociology of occupational medicine and in considerable extent has applied character. The consideration of social problems is directly related to development of general scientific knowledge and formation of concept of risk, including in medicine. The practical application of results of theoretical methodological and applied sociological studies can contribute to critical comprehension of key factors of management of occupational risks, improvement of quality of life of workers and preservation of labor longevity.

Building capacity for engagement: A scoping review of informal and formal research training for Indigenous youth.
abstract: Community-based research approaches, including community-based participatory action research (CBPAR), are a research design that engages communities as active collaborators by offering training and support throughout the research process. These approaches, including CBPAR, have gained traction in work with Indigenous youth, as they build research capacity and foster equitable partnerships between community members and researchers. As an underrepresented population in CBPAR, Indigenous youth offer critical perspectives that can deepen understanding of community needs and inform culturally responsive approaches. To explore the uptake in community-based research approaches and youth inclusion, this scoping review analyzed 37 research articles detailing 33 research training programs for Indigenous youth engaged in research in Canada, the United States, Aotearoa (New Zealand), and Australia. Training programs ranged from providing a brief overview of the research process (42%) to teaching youth specific research skills (27%). Youth involvement also varied across training programs, from being included as study participants (15%) to extensive youth co-researcher partnerships (48%). Key themes were extracted from the articles to highlight the limitations and strengths of the research training programs. title: Evaluating a Structured Self-Management Kit for Type 2 Diabetes: A Mixed Methods Service Evaluation in Primary Care.
abstract: Rationale, aims and objectives Type 2 diabetes places increasing pressure on health services, and engagement with structured education and routine preventative care remains variable. Practical self-management tools may help people translate advice into daily routines. This service evaluation examined the implementation, acceptability and early outcomes of the MyHealthKits Diabetic Wellness Kit in routine primary care. Method A prospective convergent mixed methods service evaluation was conducted across 13 general practices within three Primary Care Networks in Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent. Adults with type 2 diabetes received a Diabetic Wellness Kit containing foot care tools, educational materials and access to online resources. Health-related quality of life and healthcare use were measured at baseline and after 12 weeks using EQ-5D-5L and MODRUM questionnaires. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively, with paired EQ-5D utility change assessed using a paired t-test. Semi-structured interviews with a purposive sample explored usability and perceived impact and were analysed thematically. Results A total of 782 kits were distributed. Of these, 131 participants completed both baseline and follow-up questionnaires; three were excluded because they reported not receiving the kit, leaving 128 in the primary analysis cohort. title: Squamous Cell Carcinoma in the Diabetic Foot: A Review of Published Case Reports.
abstract: Introduction Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) is a malignant tumour arising from epidermal keratinocytes and is the second most common form of skin cancer globally. Although relatively rare on the foot, SCC and its variants may occur in people with diabetes and can mimic common diabetes-related foot ulcerations. This diagnostic overlap presents a risk of delayed recognition and treatment. The aim of this review was to synthesise published case reports of SCC occurring in the diabetic foot and to describe patient characteristics, clinical presentation, and outcomes. Methods A review of case reports was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. Electronic databases (Medline, CINAHL, SPORTDiscus and SCOPUS) were searched up to September 2025 using relevant terms for SCC and its variants. Studies describing clinical cases of SCC arising on the foot in individuals with diabetes were included. Results Thirty-one cases from 13 countries were included. The mean age of patients was 62 years, with a predominance of males (71.0%) and type 2 diabetes (64.5%). Lesions most affected the right foot (64.5%) and were frequently located on the toes or plantar surfaces. The mean lesion duration prior to diagnosis was 61.9 months (range 2-360; n = 25). Initial misdiagnosis was most commonly as a foot ulcer (54.8%), followed by a wart (19.4%) and osteomyelitis (12.9%). Final diagnoses included SCC (51.7%), verrucous carcinoma (35.5%), and Marjolin's ulcer (12.9%). Pain was reported in 58.1

title: The Lysosomal Clock: Are We Only as Old as Our Lysosomes?
abstract: Lysosomes are a major organelle involved in intracellular degradation, membrane traffic and metabolic signaling, but how their biochemical composition changes during normal aging remains poorly defined. Puszynska and colleagues now combine lysosome purification with metabolomics and lipidomics across tissues, species and ages to reveal a conserved signature of lysosomal aging characterized by accumulation of glycerophosphodiesters (GPDs) and cystine and remodeling of bis(monoacylglycero)phosphate (BMP). Strikingly, these changes are largely obscured in whole-tissue analyses and resemble metabolic abnormalities associated with lysosomal storage disorders, including CLN3 disease and cystinosis. The signature develops progressively with age, can predict chronological age, and is attenuated by caloric restriction in peripheral tissues but not in the brain. Within the brain, age-dependent metabolite accumulation is particularly prominent in microglia and is also detected in neurons, linking lysosomal aging to cell populations central to neurodegenerative disease. These findings define an organelle-level metabolic clock, suggesting that one might be only as young as one's lysosomes. Establishing whether GPDs, cystine and BMP remodeling merely mark lysosomal age or actively contribute to declining lysosomal degradation and membrane traffic may uncover a metabolic connection between physiological aging, lysosomal storage disorders and vulnerability to late-onset neurodegeneration.

title: Premature menopause and risk of type 2 diabetes among postmenopausal women: findings from the Women's Health Initiative.
abstract: Objective The association between premature menopause (age below 40 y) and subsequent risk of type 2 diabetes (T2D) is not fully understood. Sex hormone fluctuation due to ovarian function, hormone therapy (HT), and menopause-related changes in body composition may likely modify or mediate this relationship, which is the focus of this study. Methods We included 136,759 postmenopausal women aged 50-70 years from the Women's Health Initiative. Menopausal age and type (natural vs. surgery-associated) were determined using self-reported reproductive history, surgeries, menopausal symptoms, and postmenopausal HT use. T2D incidence was determined through self-reported initiation of diabetes treatment. Multivariable Cox models assessed the association between premature menopause and T2D, adjusting for demographic, lifestyle, reproductive, and health-related factors. Interaction terms were used to evaluate effect modification by HT use. Mediation analysis quantified the contribution of body mass index (BMI) to this association. Results Premature menopause (n=13,230; 9.7%) was associated with a higher risk of T2D compared with menopause at ages 50-54 (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.10; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.05-1.16). Among women with natural menopause, HT use modified the relationship between premature menopause and T2D ( Pinteraction =0.047). title: Molecular Control of Neural Stem Cell Quiescence in the Adult Zebrafish Telencephalon: Established Mechanisms and an Integrative Hypothesis.
abstract: The zebrafish telencephalon is an excellent model for adult neurogenesis under physiological and regenerative conditions, as many pathways regulating neural stem cell behavior are conserved with mammalian neurogenic niches. Resident radial glial cells (RGCs) serve as neural stem cells in the adult brain and are readily accessible in vivo, because forebrain eversion repositions the ventricular zone to the dorsal surface. Recent studies have revealed substantial heterogeneity among RGCs, including activation-primed cells and deeply quiescent states during homeostasis. Here, we first review the evidence that four mechanisms control quiescence in pallial RGCs: Notch3-mediated lateral inhibition, the neuronal bone morphogenetic protein (BMP)-Id1 axis, the nuclear receptor Nr2f1b, and the secreted factor Midkine-a. The evidence supporting them is unequal, and we state its level for each before asking whether they act together. Notch-mediated lateral inhibition and neuronal BMP-Id1 signaling converge on her4.1, the clearest documented interaction among them, whereas Nr2f1b establishes a deeper dormancy program that resists Notch and BMP inhibition and protects a reserve stem cell pool. Midkine-a is proposed to reinforce quiescence, pending functional validation. Finally, we propose as a hypothesis that these mechanisms act as partially redundant inputs whose relative contributions determine quiescence depth and vary along the antero-posterior axis of the pallium. title: On the coactions between perceived program quality and youth purpose: Toward a model of dynamic person⇔context relations.
abstract: Contemporary theories of positive youth development (PYD) emphasize dynamic, mutually beneficial relationships between individuals and their contexts as a pathway to thriving and contribution. However, there remains a critical gap in longitudinal, theory-driven research examining youth strengths (e.g., purpose) and contextual assets (e.g., program quality) in Majority World contexts, particularly within structured youth programming. The present study examined reciprocal relationships between perceived program quality (a higher-order factor of the Big Three) and youth purpose using three waves of longitudinal data from a sample of 615 adolescents (50.3% female; ages 9-16, M age = 12.5, SD age = 2.3) participating in Compassion International youth development programs in Uganda. Results using cross-lagged panel models revealed positive, reciprocal associations between perceived program quality and youth purpose, such that higher program quality predicted subsequent higher youth purpose, and stronger youth purpose predicted more positive later perceptions of program quality. Temporal precedence tests indicated that neither construct emerged as a dominant developmental driver, and therefore supported a pattern of mutual influence. These findings advance PYD theory by providing longitudinal evidence for dynamic person⇔context coactions between perceived program quality and youth purpose, consistent with dynamic, relational developmental systems perspectives.

title: Clinical Teaching Fellow Practice Within Complex Clinical-Educational Systems: An Activity Theory-Informed Case Study.
abstract: Background Clinical teaching occurs where patient care and education coexist. Within the United Kingdom's National Health Service, workforce pressures constrain teaching and supervision. Clinical Teaching Fellow (CTF) roles have expanded in response but are often viewed as discrete posts rather than practices situated within complex clinical-educational systems. This study examined how tensions within and across these systems shaped CTF practice. Methods This theory-informed exploratory qualitative case study used third-generation Activity Theory. All 10 members of a hospital medical education team were invited to a semistructured group interview; eight participated. An Activity Theory-informed thematic approach was used to map the focal undergraduate clinical education activity system and examine tensions within it and at its intersections with adjacent systems. Findings Participants included three CTFs, two education facilitators and three administrators. CTF practice involved teaching, programme coordination and administrative work within a multiprofessional team. Differing understandings of the activity's purpose and outcomes shaped practice. Professional language, continuity, experience and blurred divisions of labour influenced participation and work organisation. Relationships with clinical services, the medical school, postgraduate medical education and university-based postgraduate study introduced competing demands. title: 2025 National Guidelines on the Mediterranean Diet: Executive Summary of a Joint Report by Italian Scientific Societies and the National Institute of Health Task Force on Clinical Practice Guidelines.
abstract: Context Chronic non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are the leading global causes of morbidity, mortality, and escalating health care costs, driven largely by unhealthy lifestyles in an aging population. Objective The Mediterranean Diet (MD), traditionally associated with healthy longevity, is increasingly recognized for its preventative and therapeutic benefits across many NCDs. Data sources Using the NUTRIGRADE methodology, a multidisciplinary panel of clinical, methodological, and public health experts conducted a comprehensive systematic review across 9 health domains and one economic domain. Data extraction Data were extracted from multiple databases without date restrictions, assessing outcomes such as disease incidence and prevalence, mortality rates of nutrition-related NCDs, quality of life indicators, and relevant biochemical markers. Evidence was critically appraised and synthesized to formulate evidence-based recommendations. Data analysis A total of 84 evidence-based recommendations were developed. The MD was found to significantly reduce all-cause mortality in the general population and cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, particularly in high-risk individuals. High-quality evidence supports the protective role of the MD against myocardial infarction, stroke, atrial fibrillation, and peripheral arterial disease. In oncological evidence, MD adherence has been found to be linked to a lower incidence of several cancer types and improved survival outcomes. Additiona

title: Predictors of carotenoid status in New Zealand children using carotenoid reflection score: a cross-sectional study.
abstract: Background and objectives Optically-assessed skin carotenoid status offers an objective measure of vegetable and fruit intake. Data from the Sodium and Potassium Intake (SNaK+) study was used to explore asso-ciations of carotenoid reflection scores with body size, annual household income, vegetable and fruit intake and potassium intake, and the relationship between carotenoid reflection score and 24-h urinary potassium in children. Methods and study design Seventy-five children (29 girls, 37 boys; 9 not stated) aged 8 to 13 years from five New Zealand primary schools were supported by the parents/caregivers to complete validated questions about their frequency of vegetable and fruit intake. Carotenoid reflection scores were measured using reflection spectroscopy and 24-h urine samples (n = 69) were collected. Differences by gender and age were tested using two-sample t-tests. Linear regression identified determinants of carotenoid reflection score. title: Painful Non-Diabetic Lumbosacral Radiculoplexus Neuropathy Following Tirzepatide Exposure: A Case Report.
abstract: Background and purpose Lumbosacral radiculoplexus neuropathy (LRPN) is an uncommon neuropathic syndrome occurring predominantly in patients with diabetes mellitus, although non-diabetic forms are increasingly recognized. Rare peripheral neuropathies have been reported during glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 receptor agonist [GLP-1RA]) therapy; however, LRPN has not previously been described in this clinical context, particularly in non-diabetic individuals. We describe a well-characterized case of painful non-diabetic LRPN developing following a period of rapid metabolic shift during tirzepatide therapy. Case presentation A 62-year-old man previously treated with tirzepatide for weight loss developed, approximately 8 weeks after discontinuation, acute left-sided low back pain, rapidly progressing to severe neuropathic pain, distal weakness, and sensory loss. MR neurography demonstrated enlargement and contrast enhancement of the left L5 nerve root and sciatic nerve, associated with denervation edema. Electrophysiological studies demonstrated an axonal process consistent with lumbosacral radiculoplexus neuropathy, while cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed albuminocytological dissociation. Classical diabetic-related plexopathy was excluded by normal glucose values; an extensive work-up excluded infectious, neoplastic, paraneoplastic, and systemic inflammatory causes. title: Semaglutide-Induced Weight Loss Does Not Impair Muscle Function and Improves Endurance Running Capacity in Obese Mice.
abstract: Background Semaglutide, a member of the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, induces substantial weight loss, primarily through appetite suppression and reduced energy intake. In addition to fat mass reduction, a considerable loss of lean body mass is also observed. How these effects compare to conventional caloric restriction is unclear. The aim of the current study was to compare the effects of semaglutide injections and energy-matched caloric restriction on skeletal muscle mass, function and exercise capacity. Methods An 8-month-old high-fat diet-induced obese male C57BL/6J mice were pair-fed (n = 14), with one receiving semaglutide injections (SEMA; 30 μg/kg/day) and the other undergoing energy-matched caloric restriction (CR; sham PBS injections) for 28 days. A group of obese mice (n = 12) continued unrestricted high-fat feeding and served as controls (CON). Body mass and energy intake were monitored daily. During the final week, exercise capacity was assessed using a progressive treadmill test with oxygen consumption and lactate measurements. At study completion, mice were euthanized, and slow- and fast-twitch muscles (soleus [SOL] and extensor digitorum longus [EDL]) were dissected, weighed and used for ex vivo assessment of mechanical and contractile properties. title: Clinical Impact of the AISF STEPS-MASH Algorithm: Real-World Application in Tertiary Hepatology Practice.
abstract: Background and aims The approval of resmetirom and semaglutide for non-cirrhotic people living with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and significant fibrosis has created a need for pragmatic strategies to identify treatment candidates in routine practice. We assessed the real-world applicability of the AISF STEPS-MASH algorithm and characterised the treatment status of people reaching final assessment in tertiary hepatology centres. Methods We retrospectively applied the AISF STEPS-MASH algorithm to all consecutive adults undergoing vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) at nine Italian tertiary hepatology centres between January and June 2025. Step S defined a broad screening pool (controlled attenuation parameter [CAP] ≥ 248 dB/m and/or a metabolic referral indication). People with CAP-defined steatosis, at least one cardiometabolic risk factor or metabolic referral indication, and no documented competing liver disease aetiology were assigned to the Primary pathway; all others were analysed separately as the Non-primary pathway. Step T applied liver stiffness measurement (LSM) ≥ 8.0 kPa, excluding LSM ≥ 20.0 kPa and/or platelet count 9 /L. Step E classified safety-related conditions as label-defined contraindications, warnings requiring monitoring, or interactions requiring treatment modification or temporary deferral. title: Small Molecule-Mediated Nrf2 Activation as a Neuroprotective Approach in Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis is a chronic inflammatory autoimmune disease resulting in progressive demyelination of the central nervous system, leading to symptoms such as motor discoordination, cognitive deficits, and ocular dysfunction. Oxidative stress is a crucial component in the pathogenesis of multiple sclerosis, with reactive oxygen species contributing to myelin destruction, neuronal injury, and disruption of the blood-brain barrier resulting in symptom progression. For this reason, reducing oxidative stress has gained attention as a promising mechanism of disease control. Nuclear factor erythroid-2-related factor-2 (Nrf2) is a master regulator of the cellular antioxidant and anti-inflammatory response throughout the body, including the central nervous system. Nrf2 functions as a transcription factor to activate the expression of genes involved in detoxification and antioxidant defense, thus playing a critical role in limiting neuronal oxidative damage resulting from multiple sclerosis. Since no curative treatments are currently available for multiple sclerosis, recognizing potential new drugs that target earlier stages of the disease may be a viable strategy to intervene in disease progression and improve quality of life for the patient. This review explores how Nrf2 is a promising target for intervention in multiple sclerosis and that many Nrf2 activators exhibit robust efficacy, highlighting their potential as novel agents for multiple sclerosis treatment.

title: Ketogenic Diet Effects on Liver Health in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most prevalent chronic liver condition and is linked to unhealthy lifestyle patterns. Dietary modification remains the cornerstone of management. Among available nutritional strategies, ketogenic diets (KDs) have gained increasing attention. This systematic review evaluated the impact of KD, versus no dietary intervention or control diets, on hepatic and metabolic outcomes in adults with MASLD. Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science were searched through June 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records, assessed eligibility and extracted data. Risk of bias was evaluated using CASP for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and ROBINS-I for non-randomized studies. Meta-analysis was not feasible due to study heterogeneity. Fourteen studies were included: five RCTs and nine prospective cohorts, involving 776 adults with MASLD and/or hepatic steatosis. KD was associated with improvements in MASLD severity indices, anthropometric measures, lipid profile, glycaemic markers and liver enzymes. Among RCTs, liver fat decreased by -4.77% (PDFF) to a 77% (relative MRI-LFF), with reductions in body weight (up to -12.0 kg) and waist circumference (up to -9.6 cm). Prospective studies showed similar findings, including reductions in controlled attenuation parameter (up to -57 dB/m), intrahepatic triglyceride (-31%) and Fatty Liver Index (-14.03 points). summary_short: KD was associated with improvements in MASLD severity indices, anthropometric measures, lipid profile, glycaemic markers and liver enzymes.

title: A Murinized Bimagrumab Analogue Increases Skeletal Muscle Mass and Improves Cardiometabolic Remodelling in Experimental Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
abstract: Background Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) involves left ventricular hypertrophy and metabolic dysfunction. Given the role of skeletal muscle in systemic metabolism, we investigated whether activin type II receptor inhibition with CDD866, a murinized bimagrumab analogue that induces skeletal muscle hypertrophy, improves physical performance and cardiometabolic remodelling in established HCM. Methods Twenty-four-week-old male mice harbouring the cardiac myosin R403Q mutation received CDD866 or isotype antibody (20 mg/kg subcutaneously every 3 days) for 4 weeks; wild-type (WT) littermates received isotype antibody. Assessments included body composition, muscle imaging and histology, grip strength, treadmill exercise, glucose tolerance, echocardiography, cardiac histopathology, myocardial substrate oxidation by 13 C nuclear magnetic resonance in isolated beating hearts and cardiac transcriptomics and proteomics. Values are mean ± SEM. Results Compared with R403Q placebo, CDD866 increased lean mass (22.5 ± 0.6 vs. 18.7 ± 0.5 g; p 13 C-lactate output (15.3 ± 2.5 vs. 40.2 ± 3.8 nmol/min; p Conclusions CDD866 increased skeletal muscle mass and performance alongside improvements in cardiac remodelling, diastolic function and myocardial metabolism in established experimental HCM. title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Analog-Type Amyloidosis: A Case Report and Review of the Literature.
abstract: Abstract Amyloidosis is a heterogeneous group of diseases characterized by extracellular deposition of insoluble proteins. Glucagon-like peptide-1 analog (AGLP1)-type amyloidosis is a rare iatrogenic form of amyloidosis localized to areas of glucagon-like peptide-1 analog injections. In this study, we describe a case of AGLP1-type amyloidosis presenting as a subcutaneous mass on the abdomen of a 71-year-old woman with a history of liraglutide, semaglutide, and tirzepatide use. Biopsy, including Congo red stain, was consistent with an amyloid deposit. Amyloid protein identification by liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry showed a typical amyloid profile with low spectra for liraglutide. Immunohistochemistry, subsequently performed, showed that the amyloid deposits were positive for glucagon; there is an extensive peptide homology between liraglutide and glucagon. Only 3 cases of AGLP1-type amyloidosis have been previously reported. It is vital for clinicians and pathologists to be aware of AGLP1-type amyloidosis given the increasing worldwide use of GLP-1 agonists, as well as the potential for misdiagnosis of systemic amyloidosis, which has profound therapeutic and prognostic implications.
summary_short: Abstract Amyloidosis is a heterogeneous group of diseases characterized by extracellular deposition of insoluble proteins. Glucagon-like peptide-1 analog (AGLP1)-type amyloidosis is a rare iatrogenic form of amyloidosis localized to areas of glucagon-like peptide-1 analog injections.

title: Reductions in Advanced Chronic Liver Disease Among People Who Inject Drugs: The ETHOS Engage Study.
abstract: Background and aims Liver disease is a significant risk for people who inject drugs due to the high burden of hepatitis C virus (HCV). There is limited data on the impact of the direct-acting antiviral (DAA) therapy era on liver disease among people who inject drugs. This study evaluated baseline and longitudinal liver disease in a national cohort of people who inject drugs recruited over three Waves: 2018-2019, 2019-2021, and 2023-2025. Methods The ETHOS Engage Study is an observational cohort of people who inject drugs attending drug treatment clinics and needle and syringe programs in Australia. Participants completed a questionnaire and underwent point-of-care HCV RNA testing (Xpert HCV Viral Load Fingerstick) and liver stiffness measurement (LSM) by vibration-controlled transient hepatic elastography (FibroScan). Advanced chronic liver disease was defined by LSM of 10 kPa or above. Results Among all enrolments with a valid LSM (n = 3126, 79% recruited at drug treatment clinics), 11% had advanced chronic liver disease, decreasing from 12.0% (154/1287) in 2018-2019 to 7.9% (66/839) in 2019-2021, and 6.4% (62/967) in 2023-2025. In adjusted analyses, participants recruited between 2019-2021 and 2023-2025 were less likely to have advanced chronic liver disease (vs. 2018-2019; aOR 0.66, 95% CI: 0.48-0.90 and aOR 0.56, 95% CI: 0.40-0.77, respectively). Current HCV infection declined from 24% in 2018-2019 to 10% in 2023-2025. Among participants with LSM in more than one wave and

title: Weight-Loss Outcomes After Sleeve Gastrectomy Versus Tirzepatide in a Minority Cohort With Severe Obesity: Results From a Propensity Score Matched Cohort.
abstract: While GLP-1 and GIP receptor agonists like semaglutide and tirzepatide have revolutionized pharmacologic obesity treatment, metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS) continues to demonstrate superior weight loss and cost-effectiveness. Current evidence shows tirzepatide outperforms semaglutide with over 20% weight reduction, yet most clinical trials lack ethnic diversity, limiting the generalizability of these outcomes. This is a retrospective, single-centre study that evaluates 12-month weight loss results comparing tirzepatide and SG within a diverse, urban patient population. 12-month weight loss outcomes were compared between patients receiving tirzepatide and those undergoing sleeve gastrectomy (SG). Primary endpoints included changes in BMI, excess weight loss and total weight loss (TWL) percentage at 3, 6 and 12 months, following ASMBS reporting standards to evaluate treatment efficacy and comparative outcomes. Linear mixed models revealed statistically significant differences in weight loss between SG and tirzepatide cohorts across all time points (p 2 BMI reduction, compared to 12% TWL and 7 kg/m 2 for tirzepatide. SG was associated with greater weight loss than tirzepatide in this selected matched cohort, especially for eligible patients in ethnic minority groups. However, tirzepatide serves as a vital non-invasive alternative, requiring individualized treatment decisions based on patient preference, cost and specific metabolic goals.

title: Detection and Excretion Profile of Retatrutide in Human Plasma and Urine by LC-HRMS: Implications for Antidoping Analysis.
abstract: Rationale Retatrutide (LY3437943) is a novel long-acting triple incretin receptor agonist that targets the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R), glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor (GIPR), and glucagon receptor (GCGR). Its pronounced effects on body composition and metabolic health, combined with increasing off-label use among physically active populations, raise concerns about potential misuse in sport. Despite growing clinical interest and anecdotal reports about use among amateur athletes, information on the detection and elimination profile of retatrutide in humans remains unexplored. Methods A method based on liquid chromatography-high-resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS) dedicated to monitor retatrutide was developed and validated in human plasma and urine in accordance with World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) criteria. Detection was based on the [M + 3H] 3+ precursor ion by targeted selected-ion monitoring (t-SIM), with confirmatory analysis via parallel reaction monitoring (PRM) of structurally diagnostic fragment ions. From four retatrutide users who self-administered 2 mg subcutaneously on Days 1 and 7, blood and urine samples were collected at predefined time points following self-administration. Results The method was proved fit-for-purpose regarding selectivity, reliability, robustness, and stability. Simvastatin Alleviation of Trimethyltin-Induced Hippocampal and Behavioral Impairments via Improvement of Antioxidants, Mitochondrial Health, and Energy Homeostasis.
abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction and antioxidant deficiency are key contributors to the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Trimethyltin (TMT) induces selective hippocampal damage associated with redox disequilibrium, neuroinflammatory responses, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired energy homeostasis, leading to cognitive decline. The present study evaluated whether simvastatin as a lipid-lowering and protective medicine could mitigate TMT-induced behavioral abnormalities by improving hippocampal antioxidant status, mitochondrial integrity, and energy homeostasis. Rats were assigned to control, control + simvastatin (30 mg/kg), TMT, TMT + simvastatin (10 mg/kg), and TMT + simvastatin (30 mg/kg) groups. TMT was injected IP (once, 8 mg/kg) to instigate neurotoxicity. Following three weeks of treatment, locomotor activity and conditioned learning and memory deficits were analyzed using open-field and passive avoidance tests, respectively. Besides, hippocampal levels or activity of nitrite, glutathione (GSH), glutathione peroxidase (GPx), myeloperoxidase (MPO), and β-site APP-cleaving enzyme 1 (BACE1), mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP), and AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) were measured. Simvastatin treatment (30 mg/kg) was associated with higher latency in the passive avoidance test and longer rearing in the open field test in TMT-intoxicated rats.
