title: Barriers to Addressing Sexual Health Needs of Adults With Chronic Kidney Disease: A Multidisciplinary Survey of Renal Healthcare Professionals.
abstract: Background Sexual dysfunction is common among adults with chronic kidney disease and can significantly affect health and well-being. Understanding healthcare professionals' attitudes, training experiences, and perceived barriers toward discussing sexual health needs with patients is essential to improving patient care. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted with healthcare professionals involved in the care of adults with chronic kidney disease. The survey comprised four sections aimed to uncover participants' attitudes and beliefs toward sexual health, experience of sexual health training and practice, and barriers to discussing sexual health. Recruitment and data collection were conducted through social media and professional renal networks between December 2022 and April 2023. Descriptive statistics (means, standard deviations, frequencies, and percentages) were employed to summarise responses. Bivariate analyses were conducted to examine differences in sexual health attitude and belief scores across participants' age, sex, and professional experience. Open-ended responses were summarised descriptively. Results A total of 135 participants completed the survey. Most were female nurses aged 35-54, working in haemodialysis, with more than 10 years' experience. Almost 80% had not received any sexual health training in their current or previous roles. The average attitude score was 35.49 ± 6.95, suggesting a relatively positive attitude. Ninety percent believed that add
summary_short: Background Sexual dysfunction is common among adults with chronic kidney disease and can significantly affect health and well-being. Understanding healthcare professionals' attitudes, training experiences, and perceived barriers toward discussing sexual health needs with patients is essential to improving patient care.

title: The Association of Early Graft Dysfunction and CYP3A5 Genotype With Tacrolimus Exposure in Adult Kidney Transplant Recipients.
abstract: Introduction The incidence of early graft dysfunction following kidney transplantation is rising due to the expanded use of marginal organs. Prior studies have suggested that acute kidney dysfunction causes renohepatic crosstalk and tacrolimus metabolism may be decreased. It is also well known that tacrolimus metabolism and dosing requirements differ significantly based on a recipient's CYP3A5 genotype. The objective of this study was to investigate the interplay between early graft function and pharmacogenetics on tacrolimus dose requirements in adult kidney transplant recipients. Methods This was a single-center, retrospective cohort study of adult kidney transplant recipients who received immediate-release tacrolimus and had CYP3A5 genotypes available. Immediate graft function (IGF) was defined as serum creatinine decrease of ≥ 10% from baseline and urine output ≥ 0.5 mL/kg/h on post-operative day (POD) 1. Tacrolimus dose-normalized trough concentration (C/D) on POD 2 was compared between patients with IGF and non-IGF using Mann-Whitney U test. Patients were then grouped by both IGF and CYP3A5 genotype, and the differences in C/D considering these factors were analyzed by Mann Whitney U test and a multivariable linear regression analysis. Results A total of 242 patients were included, 185 with IGF and 57 with non-IGF. The median [IQR: interquartile range] of tacrolimus C/D was higher in non-IGF than IGF (200.0 [129.7-327.1] vs. 134.0 [95.0-197.4] [ng/ml]/[mg/kg/day], p Con
summary_short: Introduction The incidence of early graft dysfunction following kidney transplantation is rising due to the expanded use of marginal organs. Prior studies have suggested that acute kidney dysfunction causes renohepatic crosstalk and tacrolimus metabolism may be decreased.

title: Industry Perspective on Current Guidelines, Challenges, and Future Directions for ADME Characterization of Payloads for Antibody-Drug Conjugates.
abstract: A total of 15 antibody-drug conjugates (ADC)s have been approved by USFDA till December 2025 with the use of nine cytotoxic payload molecules. Small molecule payloads can undergo enzymatic or nonenzymatic biotransformation, distribution, protein or red blood cell binding, transporter mediated disposition and urinary and/or biliary-fecal excretion. Existing regulatory framework suggests payloads to be characterized for absorption, distribution, metabolism and elimination (ADME) like small molecule therapeutics. Additionally, drug-drug interactions (DDI) relevant investigations are imperative for the payloads. This review focuses on different approaches sponsors have adopted to address payload specific ADME-DDI questions. The comparison of ADME characteristics of nine approved payloads is presented. It is pointed out that because of lack of ADC specific guidance from regulators, as well as novelty of the ADC platforms, there is no uniformity in addressing ADME properties of payloads, and noticeable differences in approaching the necessity of providing clinical drug interaction data. As ADCs evolve, and more payloads are being developed, the regulatory framework will also need to evolve to guide developers.
summary_short: Existing regulatory framework suggests payloads to be characterized for absorption, distribution, metabolism and elimination (ADME) like small molecule therapeutics.

title: The Place of Therapeutic Apheresis in Severe Immune-Related Adverse Events: A Scoping Review of Literature.
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized the management of patients with cancer. However, they can induce breakdowns in immunologic tolerance, leading to autoimmune diseases, or immune related adverse events (irAEs). These irAEs can sometimes be life threatening, requiring aggressive management, such as immunosuppressant (IS) or even therapeutic apheresis (TA). TA, an extracorporeal circulation technique, may represent a therapeutic option for severe irAEs, reducing their severity and duration by removing ICIs, pathogenic antibodies or inflammatory cytokines, although its role in this situation remains underreported. We made scoping review to better identify the use of TA for managing severe irAEs. From January 2022 to August 2025, three databases were reviewed, for articles mentioning the use of TA in the event of immunotoxicity. Only case reports or case series were retained. A descriptive summary was produced in table forms. Between 2022 and 2025, 162 articles were identified, 34 articles concerning 42 patients treated for severe irAE via TA were included. The underlying cancers were mainly non-small cell lung cancer and melanoma, and 78% of patients were treated with monotherapy anti-PD(L)1. The main indications for TA were neurological (40.6%), overlap manifestations (23.8%), and hepatitis (21.4%), mainly highly severe. TA was most often used in rescue situations, that is, after failure of several lines of IS. Complications of TA were rare. Clinical improv
summary_short: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized the management of patients with cancer. However, they can induce breakdowns in immunologic tolerance, leading to autoimmune diseases, or immune related adverse events (irAEs).

title: Aquaporin-4 Orchestrates Muscle Cell Differentiation and Satellite Cell Preservation: A Novel Target in Age-Related Muscle Decline.
abstract: Background Impaired muscle regeneration is a key contributor to age-related muscle decline, yet the molecular mechanisms linking muscle water homeostasis to regenerative failure remain incompletely understood. Aquaporin-4 (AQP4), a major skeletal muscle water channel, may have functions beyond water transport that are relevant to muscle maintenance and repair. We investigated whether altered AQP4 expression contributes to age-related defects in skeletal muscle regeneration and whether AQP4 may represent a targetable pathway for muscle dysfunction associated with ageing. Methods Skeletal muscle from young adult (25-week; n = 9) and aged (85-week; n = 8) rats was analysed for extracellular and intracellular water content by bioimpedance. AQP4, AQP1 and myogenic markers were measured by Western blot. Satellite cells isolated from skeletal muscle were assessed for proliferation, differentiation and expression of differentiation markers. To define the mechanistic role of AQP4 in myogenesis, CRISPR-generated AQP4-silenced L6 rat myoblasts were evaluated for proliferation, differentiation, senescence and Akt/PKB signalling. Rescue experiments were performed by restoring AQP4 expression in silenced cells. Data are reported as mean ± SEM. title: Fracture incidence and mortality in kidney transplant recipients compared with waitlisted dialysis patients: A single-center retrospective analysis.
abstract: Aims Kidney transplantation (KT) improves survival in end-stage renal disease (ESRD); however, the post-transplant fracture risk remains uncertain. This study aimed to compare the fracture incidence between kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) and waitlisted dialysis patients and to examine the association between fracture events and all-cause mortality in each group. Materials and methods This study included a single-center cohort of 504 KTRs and 423 waitlisted dialysis patients treated at a tertiary hospital in South Korea from 1998 to 2019. Fractures were identified through radiological report review, and mortality data were retrieved from medical records. Multivariate Cox regression models were used to evaluate mortality predictors, including fracture events, as covariates. Results The fracture incidence did not differ significantly between KTRs (9.1%) and dialysis patients (12.5%). Moreover, fractures were not significantly associated with increased mortality in either group (KTRs: hazard ratio (HR), 2.03; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.62 - 6.67; p = 0.24; dialysis: HR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.12 - 8.08; p = 0.98). Age was the strongest mortality predictor. Among KTRs, tacrolimus use was associated with lower mortality compared with cyclosporine (HR, 0.18; 95% CI, 0.05 - 0.66; p = 0.009). Conclusion KTRs have a fracture risk comparable to that of dialysis patients, and fractures were not significantly associated with mortality. The survival benefits of KT are driven by factors
summary_short: Among KTRs, tacrolimus use was associated with lower mortality compared with cyclosporine (HR, 0.18; 95% CI, 0.05 - 0.66; p = 0.009). Conclusion KTRs have a fracture risk comparable to that of dialysis patients, and fractures were not significantly associated with mortality.

title: Survival From Profound Acidemia (pH <6.8) in Metformin-Associated Lactic Acidosis: The Critical Role of Early Recognition With Early Dialysis.
abstract: Metformin-associated lactic acidosis (MALA) is a rare but potentially fatal complication of metformin therapy, particularly in patients with renal impairment. Despite its rarity, MALA carries significant mortality risk and requires prompt recognition and treatment. We report a case of severe MALA in a 67-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus and progressive neurocognitive decline who presented with altered mental status, severe metabolic acidosis, and acute kidney injury. Laboratory findings revealed profound lactic acidosis (lactate 22 mmol/L, peak 24 mmol/L), severe acidemia (pH <6.8), acute renal failure (creatinine 8.73 mg/dL), and a markedly elevated serum metformin level of 74 mcg/mL (reference range 1-2 mcg/mL). Collateral history suggested possible metformin toxicity. The patient was treated with continuous venovenous hemodiafiltration (CVVHDF), mechanical ventilation, and vasopressor support. She recovered fully with normalization of renal function and return to baseline neurological status by discharge. This case highlights the importance of medication reconciliation in patients with cognitive im- pairment, adherence to sick-day medication rules, and the critical role of early renal replacement therapy in MALA management. Despite the extremely elevated metformin level and severe acidemia, the patient achieved complete recovery, demonstrating the reversibility of MALA with appropriate intervention.
summary_short: We report a case of severe MALA in a 67-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus and progressive neurocognitive decline who presented with altered mental status, severe metabolic acidosis, and acute kidney injury.

Integrated transcriptomic and metabolite analysis reveals the role of AktADT8 in the biosynthesis of phenylalanine and its derivatives in Akebia trifoliata.
abstract: Arogenate dehydratase (ADT) is a key enzyme in plant phenylalanine (Phe) biosynthesis, providing precursors for protein and phenolic compounds. Akebia trifoliata is valued as a medicinal, fruit, and ornamental plant because of its abundance of Phe and derivatives. Among the 373 metabolites identified previously, 135 were phenolic compounds. Furthermore, analysis of 153 transcriptomic datasets from 53 samples across nine BioProjects revealed that AktADT3 and AktADT8 exhibited obvious stage-specific expression patterns. A total of 758 mutation sites were detected in AktADTs, with AktADT8 displaying a markedly higher proportion of synonymous variants. Co-expression analysis indicated that AktADT transcript abundance correlated significantly with the levels of 124 metabolites and 150 enzyme-encoding genes across five flavonoid biosynthesis pathways, with AktADT8 uniquely showing broad positive correlations across all pathways. Overexpression of AktADT6 and AktADT8 in Arabidopsis transformant lines presented significantly increased contents of Phe and flavonoids. Moreover, AktADT8 was uniquely characterized by two transcription start sites, and binding prediction suggested that MYB105 (where MYB is v-myb avian myeloblastosis viral oncogene homolog) could bind to the promoter region of AktADT8, whereas MYB21 could bind to the promoter regions of both AktADT8 and AktADTs8, thereby regulating their transcriptional activity. title: <b>Glycated hemoglobin and retinal microvascular changes in type 2 diabetic retinopathy patients treated with metformin and/or insulin: A retrospective study</b>.
abstract: Background Diabetes retinopathy (DR) is the main blinding complication of type 2 diabetes (T2DM). Glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) can reflect long-term blood glucose control and optical coherence tomography (OCT) can evaluate retinal microvessels. The effects of metformin and insulin regimens on microvascular structure are not yet clear. Objectives To explore the relationship between HbA1c levels and retinal microvascular changes in T2DM patients receiving metformin and/or insulin and to evaluate the impact of different hypoglycemic regimens on DR progression. Methods This retrospective study included T2DM patients with non‑proliferative DR treated between January 2023 and December 2024. After propensity score matching (PSM), 31 patients per group received metformin monotherapy (M), insulin‑based therapy (Ins), or combined therapy (M‑Ins). HbA1c, HbA1c variability (HbA1c‑SD), DR grade, central macular thickness (CMT), retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness and superficial/deep capillary plexus (SCP/DCP) density were recorded at baseline, 1‑ and 2‑year follow‑up. Multiple linear regression and Cox regression were used. Results After 2 years, HbA1c and HbA1c‑SD decreased significantly in all groups (p 0.05). title: Synthetic Data in MR Spectroscopy: Current Practices, Applications, and Considerations.
abstract: Synthetic data generation has become an increasingly important component of methodological development in magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS), particularly in contexts where ground-truth in vivo measurements are limited, noisy, or inaccessible. This review provides a structured overview of current practices in synthetic MRS data generation, with emphasis on the physical, biochemical, and computational assumptions that underpin commonly used models. A decomposition of synthetic MRS data is presented in terms of core building blocks, including basis sets, signal formation models, and metabolite parameter distributions such as concentration and relaxation properties. This framework is extended to advanced components required for realistic data synthesis, including baseline and nuisance signals, spatial encoding effects such as coil sensitivities and field inhomogeneities, k-space sampling and gradient imperfections, as well as sample-specific and temporal dynamics. Beyond single-voxel modeling, synthetic data generation across multiple MRS modalities is discussed, including functional MRS, diffusion-weighted MRS, and spectroscopic imaging, with emphasis on modality-specific challenges such as physiological variability, motion, and confounding signal contributions. summary_short: This framework is extended to advanced components required for realistic data synthesis, including baseline and nuisance signals, spatial encoding effects such as coil sensitivities and field inhomogeneities, k-space sampling and gradient imperfections, as well as sample-specific and temporal dynamics.

title: Radiation-Induced Liver Disease: From Mechanistic Paradigms to Systems-Level Prevention and Management.
abstract: Radiation-induced liver disease (RILD) is a critical dose-limiting toxicity of abdominal tumour radiotherapy. Non-classical RILD (ncRILD)-characterized by poorly understood mechanisms, a paucity of biomarkers and limited therapeutic strategies-poses an urgent clinical challenge. Building on a systematic review of differences in clinical phenotypes, pathological processes and established mechanisms such as reactive oxygen species (ROS) overload-mediated DNA damage between classical and ncRILD, this review provides a comprehensive integration and in-depth analysis of three emerging pathogenic mechanisms: (1) m 6 A epigenetic modification drives innate immune dysregulation through the ALKBH5-HMGB1-STING axis (functionally validated in RILD models); (2) epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) emerges as a top-ranked hub protein in irradiated liver sinusoidal endothelial cells, suggesting a reversal from a protective signal to a pro-injury switch (proteomic evidence; functional validation pending); and (3) a proposed crosstalk among taurine metabolic dysregulation, ferroptosis and disulfidptosis, which may clarify the role of metabolic cell death in RILD progression (theoretical hypothesis). The review further analyzes bidirectional interactions between RILD and the liver microenvironment, tumour microenvironment and immune response and constructs an end-to-end management framework encompassing pharmacological prevention and treatment, precision radiotherapy and the three-tier pre

title: Most severe TAFRO syndrome without proven iMCD responded to combination therapy with glucocorticoids, tocilizumab, rituximab and sirolimus: A Case Report.
abstract: TAFRO syndrome is a systemic inflammatory disease without established treatment strategy. Treatment generally involves immunosuppressive therapy, primarily with glucocorticoids and tocilizumab. A 45-year-old woman initially developed cough and fever, then worsening generalized fatigue. After failing to respond to antibiotics and becoming anuric, hemodialysis was initiated. The patient had marked pleural and abdominal effusions, hepatosplenomegaly, thrombocytopenia, markedly elevated inflammatory markers, hypoalbuminemia, renal dysfunction, and coagulation abnormalities. Bone marrow examination revealed megakaryocytosis and reticulofibrosis, so she met the diagnostic criteria for TAFRO syndrome. Although a lymph node biopsy could not be performed, the patient met other diagnostic criteria for idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease, and we diagnosed TAFRO with probable idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease. She also developed disseminated intravascular coagulation and was identified with the most severe form of TAFRO syndrome (severity Grade 5). High-dose glucocorticoids were started with tocilizumab and rituximab. However, there was little improvement in the patient's general condition, so we added sirolimus, an mTOR inhibitor. After that, a marked clinical response was observed and dialysis was discontinued. Remission was achieved through the continuation of glucocorticoids, tocilizumab, rituximab, and sirolimus. title: Non-Intestinal Adenocarcinoma Centered in the Middle Ear With Focal Mucinous Differentiation: A Rare Case Managed With Surgery and Adjuvant Radiotherapy.
abstract: A 68-year-old man with longstanding unilateral hearing loss and persistent otorrhoea was found to have a rare non-intestinal adenocarcinoma with focal mucinous differentiation centered in the middle ear. He underwent mastoidectomy and tympanomastoid surgery followed by adjuvant radiotherapy. More than 5 years later, he remains disease-free with persistent hearing loss.
summary_short: A 68-year-old man with longstanding unilateral hearing loss and persistent otorrhoea was found to have a rare non-intestinal adenocarcinoma with focal mucinous differentiation centered in the middle ear.

title: The gut‒kidney axis.
abstract: Gut-kidney dialog is integral to the holobiont. This review explores the interactions between these two organ-systems across physicochemical, endocrine, immune, and metabolic levels. It is argued that the gut makes physiological concessions favoring the microbiota, which must be assured by the kidneys, extending the concept of renal homeostasis to holostasis . When considering pathological situations, three dimensions of the gut‒kidney axis are identified: (1) the gut causing kidney disease, (2) the effect of renal failure on the gut, and (3) the systemic effects of the gut in renal failure. Causal roles of the gut in enteric hyperoxaluria, IgA nephropathy and diabetic nephropathy are described. The impact of a uremic environment on the gut is discussed. Conversely the intestinal origins of uremic toxins and their impact on distant organs, including the kidneys themselves, are outlined. Special consideration is given to host-microbiota immune interactions, immunosuppressive therapy and kidney transplantation. Therapeutic interventions targeting the gut-kidney axis are appraised.
summary_short: Gut-kidney dialog is integral to the holobiont. This review explores the interactions between these two organ-systems across physicochemical, endocrine, immune, and metabolic levels.

title: Recognition and management of semaglutide overdose and intoxi​cation: a narrative review for clinicians.
abstract: Semaglutide has moved within a few years from a niche glucose-lowering agent to one of the most widely dispensed medicines in high-income countries, and reported excessive exposures have risen in parallel. This review sets out a practical framework for recognising and managing semaglutide overdose, and distinguishes recommendations supported by published overdose evidence from those resting on pharmacological reasoning or general toxicology practice. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase and Web of Science were searched from January 2005 to July 2026 for English-language human studies of semaglutide pharmacology, safety and excessive exposure, supplemented by reference lists and regulatory agency publications. Randomised trials and meta-analyses were prioritised for statements about incidence; case reports, case series and poison centre or pharmacovigilance analyses informed the description of the overdose syndrome itself. The dominant toxidrome is gastrointestinal and protracted, with nausea, repetitive vomiting, abdominal pain and anorexia persisting for days to weeks because the terminal elimination half-life approaches one week. Volume depletion, electrolyte derangement and acute kidney injury drive serious outcome. Hypoglycaemia is uncommon in isolated overdose because insulinotropic action is glucose-dependent, but it matters with concomitant insulin or sulfonylurea therapy, in non-diabetic individuals, and where a falsified product contains insulin. title: Electrical pulse stimulation of skeletal muscle in vitro: A systematic review of the methods used to mimic exercise.
abstract: Background The use of electrical pulse stimulation (EPS) as a method to induce contractions in cultured skeletal muscle has experienced rapid growth in recent years. Despite evidence demonstrating its utility in replicating some acute and chronic adaptations to exercise observed in vivo, there is a lack of evidence concerning the optimal parameters necessary to induce specific molecular adaptations. Methods This systematic review adhered to the Preferred Reporting Systems for Systematic Reviews. Eligible studies were published in English within peer-reviewed articles. Searches were executed in three databases, with an additional search for grey literature conducted on Google Scholar. Studies investigating chronic EPS in C2C12, and primary human muscle cells were incorporated. Results One hundred and twenty-seven studies spanning over twenty years of research fulfilled the criteria of this review. Outcome measures were categorised into distinct groups: Morphology, gene expression, protein abundance and/or activity, mitochondrial content/function, contractile function, metabolic changes, and cell viability. Conclusions EPS is effective in inducing a generalised exercise-like response in cultured muscle cells. However, unlike exercise in vivo, the observed molecular responses divergent in endurance/resistance exercises do not occur. title: Minimally genotoxic conditioning increases donor chimerism in a mismatched murine transplant model for sickle cell disease.
abstract: Sickle cell disease (SCD) causes severe complications, organ damage, and premature death, with hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) being the only curative option. Myeloablative conditioning (MAC) is used for traditional allogeneic HCT and autologous gene therapies, but it is often too toxic for adults with organ damage. Non-myeloablative (NMA) haploidentical HCT can expand the donor pool and be applied to patients with organ impairment. Still, two major concerns face NMA haploidentical HCT: graft failure and recipient-derived hematologic malignancies. Therefore, our aim has shifted towards maximizing donor chimerism levels. This work explores non-genotoxic antibody-based conditioning in a mismatched murine HCT model for SCD. We targeted two cell-surface receptors: CD45, a pan-hematopoietic cell marker, and CD117, a receptor expressed mainly on hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells. Saporin (sap), the drug payload, is released intracellularly, halting protein synthesis and inducing cell death. Our base conditioning regimen also included post-transplant cyclophosphamide (PT-Cy) and sirolimus. We utilized an allogeneic murine HCT model in which female donor Balb/c bone marrow (BM) cells were transplanted into female C57Bl/6J recipients. Peripheral blood (PB) analysis showed that conjugated antibodies successfully induced mixed chimerism, whereas the naked version failed. title: Retrospective cohort analysis of spontaneous regression in pediatric lymphatic malformations and its role in modern multidisciplinary approach.
abstract: Background Lymphatic malformations (LMs) often require active treatment, including sclerotherapy, surgery, or sirolimus. However, some lesions regress spontaneously, and factors associated with spontaneous regression remain incompletely undefined. In this study, we aimed to investigate the incidence, timing, and predictors of spontaneous regression in pediatric LMs. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 118 patients diagnosed with LMs before 20 years of age and by 2025 who had documented outpatient follow-up and/or treatment at our institution between January 2007 and April 2026. Spontaneous regression was defined as a >50% reduction in lesion volume without standard LMs-directed treatment, with no clinically significant symptoms, only minimal residual cosmetic concern, and no active treatment considered necessary; regression was confirmed by MRI in all cases. Logistic regression was performed to identify associated factors. Cumulative incidence of spontaneous regression was estimated using a competing-risks approach, with initiation of LMs-directed treatment before regression as a competing event. Results Spontaneous regression occurred in 43 of 118 patients (36.4%), including 33 of 59 macrocystic lesions (55.9%) versus 10 of 59 non-macrocystic lesions (16.9%). title: Topical tacrolimus achieves clinical remission but only marginally delays onset of advanced therapy in chronic proctitis: a dual center retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Background Topical tacrolimus (TT) is an off-label treatment for chronic refractory proctitis and may represent an alternative to advanced therapies, which can be limited by costs, systemic adverse effects, and patient preferences. However, evidence regarding its ability to delay escalation to advanced therapies is limited. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study at two Danish IBD centers and included all patients with ulcerative proctitis treated with TT between 2022 and 2025. Treatment efficacy was assessed by bowel movements and rectal bleeding before and after treatment. Remission was defined as Results Thirteen patients were included, receiving 17 courses of TT (duration 8 weeks) with a median follow-up of 644 days (IQR 447-779). Clinical remission at the end of treatment was achieved in 9 (53%) courses. Bowel movements decreased significantly in patients attaining remission (from 6 to 1 vs. 6 to 6, p = 0.01), as did the proportion of patients reporting rectal bleeding (78% to 0% vs. 75% to 50%, p = 0.009) and fecal calprotectin (465 mg/kg to 74 vs. 295 mg/kg to 1,470, p = 0.03). title: Effects of Liraglutide as Add-on to Metformin on Hepatic Steatosis and Fibrosis in Patients with Prediabetes and MASLD: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Background and aims The coexistence of prediabetes and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is common and accelerates metabolic and hepatic complications. This study evaluated the effects of liraglutide on hepatic steatosis and fibrosis in patients with prediabetes and MASLD. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 263 patients with prediabetes and MASLD who received either liraglutide plus metformin (liraglutide group, n=142) or metformin alone (control group, n=121) for 12 months. Primary outcomes were changes in controlled attenuation parameter (CAP), liver stiffness measurement (LSM), Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index, and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease fibrosis score (NFS). title: Research progress and clinical prospects of sonodynamic therapy in cancer treatment.
abstract: Sonodynamic therapy (SDT) uses ultrasound and a sensitizer to generate cytotoxic chemistry at depths inaccessible to most light-based treatments. Nanomaterial studies have broadened this idea from local reactive oxygen species (ROS) production to delivery, microenvironment remodeling, and immune priming, while published human studies remain small. This focused narrative review connects acoustic and sensitizer mechanisms to three interacting barriers: oxygen scarcity limits some ROS routes, glutathione-centered defenses buffer oxidative injury, and an immunosuppressive niche interrupts the passage from tumor injury to effective immunity. We compare representative oxygen-supplying, redox-active, and immunomodulatory platforms according to the mechanism and model tested and distinguish markers of regulated cell death from experiments that establish causal contribution. In animals, SDT with checkpoint blockade has controlled untreated lesions in selected models, but immune biomarkers, distant-lesion effects, and rechallenge protection are separate levels of evidence. Early glioma reports using 5-aminolevulinic acid or other porphyrin sensitizers provide tissue pharmacodynamic and safety observations alongside a small pilot with predominantly progressive disease; none establishes a survival benefit. title: Impact of Semaglutide on Cardiovascular Risk - Investigation of the Japanese Population in the SELECT Trial.
abstract: Background In the international SELECT trial (NCT03574597), the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist semaglutide reduced the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) by 20% vs. placebo in individuals with overweight/obesity (body mass index ≥27 kg/m 2 ) without diabetes. This exploratory subgroup analysis of the SELECT dataset investigated the effect of semaglutide on cardiovascular outcomes in Japanese individuals (Japanese population) and an indication population meeting Japanese criteria for subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg for the treatment of obesity. Methods and results Participants were randomly allocated to once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg or placebo, alongside standard of care. The primary cardiovascular endpoint was time to first event adjudication committee-confirmed MACE. There were 357 participants (semaglutide, n=177; placebo, n=180) in the Japanese population and 15,903 (semaglutide, n=7,963; placebo, n=7,940) in the indication population. In the Japanese population, MACE were observed in 10 and 16 participants in the semaglutide and placebo groups, respectively (hazard ratio 0.61; 95% confidence interval 0.27-1.32), directionally consistent with the SELECT population. MACE risk reduction in the indication population followed a similar trend. Changes in secondary cardiovascular and metabolic outcomes favored semaglutide over placebo in both populations. title: Effects of Calorie Restriction and AMPK Modulation on Complete Blood Count Parameters in High-Fat-Diet-Induced Metabolic Syndrome.
abstract: Background : Metabolic syndrome (MetS) is a complex systemic disorder involving metabolic dysfunction, chronic low-grade inflammation, and increased cardiovascular risk. Hematological alterations may reflect these systemic disturbances and could provide easily accessible markers of disease progression and response to intervention. This study investigated the effects of a high-fat diet (HFD) and subsequent calorie restriction (CR) on hematological parameters and derived inflammatory indices while exploring the potential involvement of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) signaling. Methods : Eight-week-old male Wistar-Kyoto rats were divided into four groups ( n = 9-10/group): CTRL, standard diet for 10 weeks; HFD, 42% high-fat diet for 10 weeks; HFD-CR, 6 weeks of HFD followed by 4 weeks of CR (20% for 2 weeks and 35% for last 2 weeks); and HFD-CR-CC, the same HFD-CR protocol combined with Compound C (1.5 mg/kg, i.p., twice weekly during CR) to inhibit AMPK. Metabolic and biometric parameters, as well as complete blood count (CBC), were recorded. Derived inflammatory indices were calculated from CBC values. Results : HFD induced metabolic alterations accompanied by CBC changes including changes in leukocyte profiles, decreased erythrocyte parameters (erythrocyte count, hematocrit, and hemoglobin concentration), and altered platelet indices. title: Comparative genomic scans identify putative immune-associated candidate regions in Indian indicine cattle compared with European taurine cattle.
abstract: Indian indicine cattle are adapted to diverse tropical production environments, but the genomic basis of these adaptive and immune-related traits remains incompletely understood. Whole-genome sequencing data from 34 animals representing seven Indian indicine breeds were compared with data from 30 European taurine cattle representing the Holstein-Friesian and Jersey breeds. Because evolutionary lineage, geographic origin and indigenous/exotic status were confounded in the sampling design, the comparative analyses primarily represent indicine-taurine genomic differentiation. Inter-population selection-signature analyses based on the fixation index (F ST ) and cross-population extended haplotype homozygosity (XP-EHH) identified 825 candidate genes within highly differentiated regions and 500 candidate genes within regions showing positive normalized XP-EHH scores in the indicine group. F ST candidate genes showed nominal associations with metabolic and immune-related pathways; however, none remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction. In contrast, eight KEGG pathways associated with XP-EHH candidate genes remained significant after correction (BH-adjusted P < 0.05), including natural killer cell-mediated cytotoxicity, complement and coagulation cascades, graft-versus-host disease, ABC transporters, allograft rejection, folate transport and metabolism, and antifolate resistance. title: Effects of a Microbiome-Targeted Diet on Cardiometabolic Risk in People Living With HIV: A Randomized Controlled Trial With Mediation Analysis.
abstract: Background Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a leading cause of morbidity among people living with HIV (PLWH), partly driven by gut microbiome dysbiosis. Whether microbiome-targeted dietary interventions can reduce CVD risk in this population remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a microbiome-targeted dietary intervention on CVD risk and gut microbiome in PLWH and to examine potential microbial mediation. Methods We conducted a 12-week, single-blind, parallel-group randomized controlled trial in PLWH with elevated CVD risk in China. Participants were assigned to a microbiome-targeted diet (n = 29), consisting of a culturally adapted, polyphenol-rich dietary pattern supplemented with Spirulina , or a control group receiving standard dietary advice (n = 31). The primary outcome was 10-year CVD risk estimated via pooled cohort equations (PCE). Secondary outcomes included cardiometabolic biomarkers and gut microbiota profiles assessed by 16S rRNA sequencing. Exploratory mediation analyses were conducted to evaluate indirect associations involving microbial taxa. title: Neuromodulation of cortical networks facilitates motor generalization of balance training in older adults
abstract: Motor generalization, the ability to transfer learned motor skills to untrained contexts, declines with aging and limits the functional benefits of rehabilitation. Although transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation (tVNS) has been implicated in neuroplasticity, its potential to facilitate motor generalization and associated cortical network reorganization in older adults remains unclear. Forty community-dwelling older adults (69.2 ± 4.3 years) were randomly assigned to receive either tVNS ( n = 20) or sham stimulation ( n = 20) during stabilometer balance training. Motor generalization was assessed on the day following training using an untrained foam-stance task. Postural regulation was characterized using center-of-pressure (COP) measures, stabilogram diffusion analysis, a composite control index (CCI), and sample entropy (SampEn). Cortical network organization was examined using beta-band electroencephalography (EEG) functional connectivity and minimum spanning tree (MST) analysis. Compared with sham stimulation, tVNS-assisted training produced greater improvements in COP area, accompanied by changes in postural dynamics, CCI, and SampEn. MST analyses revealed increased leaf fraction and reduced average eccentricity and network diameter, although baseline-adjusted analyses provided the most consistent support for average eccentricity. title: Blood-derived dietary protein promotes sleep in the mosquito Aedes aegypti
abstract: Sleep is a ubiquitous, yet highly variable, behavior across species. The duration and timing of sleep are influenced by ecological demands and dietary context. In the mosquito Aedes aegypti , a blood-feeding insect with specialized nutritional requirements, the relationship between feeding and sleep remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated how blood-derived dietary protein influences sleep regulation. Using postural analysis, videography, and arousal-threshold assays, we established that immobility bouts of ≥10 min reliably define sleep in A. aegypti . Mosquitoes lacking the circadian clock gene cycle still maintained daily sleep rhythms but exhibited reduced sleep duration and heightened overall activity. Infrared activity monitoring revealed that blood-fed females showed a marked increase in sleep beginning immediately after feeding and persisting for several days, accompanied by reduced locomotor activity. Notably, this sleep elevation lasted well beyond the cessation of previously reported host-seeking phases, raising the possibility of distinct phases of opportunistic vs. targeted host pursuit. To determine the dietary basis of this effect, we tested mosquitoes fed a bovine serum albumin (BSA)-based diet. BSA feeding alone was sufficient to mimic the sleep-promoting and activity-reducing effects of blood, suggesting dietary protein is a major nutritional regulator. title: Interfacial gap formation in deep occlusal bulk-fill resin composite restorations: A comparison of semi-split delayed gap closure and conventional bulk filling techniques using microcomputed tomography.
abstract: Polymerization shrinkage in bulk-fill resin composite restorations can lead to interfacial gap formation in deep occlusal cavities, compromising restoration integrity and longevity. Whether the semi-split delayed gap closure method reduces gap formation over conventional bulk filling is unclear. The purpose of this in vitro study was to compare the effect of the semi-split delayed gap closure and the conventional bulk filling technique on interfacial gap formation in deep occlusal bulk-fill resin composite restorations using microcomputed tomography (µCT). Tetric N-Etch etching gel, Tetric N-Bond Universal adhesive, and Tetric N-Ceram Bulk Fill resin composite (Ivoclar AG) were used for all adhesive and restorative procedures. Standardized Class I, square-shaped cavities (3×3 mm and 4 mm deep) were prepared in 24 extracted human molars. Specimens were allocated into 2 groups according to the restorative technique used (n=12 per group): an experimental group and a control group. In the experimental group, cavities were restored using the semi-split delayed gap closure technique. A 4-mm bulk of bulk-fill resin composite was placed in each cavity, and a diagonal gap (1.5 mm wide×2.0 mm deep) was created in the unpolymerized resin composite bulk, followed by initial light polymerization. Fermented Foods Target Multiple Hallmarks of Aging to Promote Healthy Longevity.
abstract: Aging is associated with progressive physiological decline driven by chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, immune dysfunction, and gut microbial dysbiosis, and fermented foods contain probiotics and bioactive metabolites that may beneficially influence these processes. This narrative review summarizes evidence on fermented foods and mechanisms associated with healthy aging, particularly gut microbiota composition, immune function, oxidative stress, and inflammation, while explicitly distinguishing findings from cell-based (in vitro) systems, animal (in vivo) models, and human participants. Each finding is labeled by its evidence tier so the strength and translational relevance of the data can be judged transparently. In vitro studies using cultured cells, including senescent fibroblasts, immune cells, and cancer cell lines, show that fermentation-derived metabolites can activate antioxidant, autophagic, and anti-inflammatory signaling pathways, and studies in rodent models, principally aged mice, show that fermented foods and their metabolites can improve mitochondrial function, reduce inflammatory markers, and reshape the gut microbiota. title: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular longevity-what is established, what is hypothesis?
abstract: Cardiovascular aging is the rate-limiting process for human life expectancy and healthspan. Nutrition and metabolism are the most widely available geroprotective targets, yet the underlying evidence is markedly uneven. To define which nutritional and metabolic interventions are established for cardiovascular longevity, or better healthy aging, and which remain hypothetical. Narrative review of randomized trials, cohort studies, and mechanistic work on dietary patterns, energy balance, meal timing, food quality, supplements, and biomarkers of biological aging. Whole dietary patterns (Mediterranean, "Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension" [DASH], sodium reduction) reduce hard cardiovascular endpoints, and the causal roles of apolipoprotein B (apoB)-containing lipoproteins, blood pressure, and adiposity are firmly established. Pharmacologically induced weight loss via glucagon-like peptide‑1 (GLP-1)-based drugs reduces cardiovascular events to a degree not achieved by lifestyle programs, shifting clinical nutrition toward preservation of lean mass and micronutrient adequacy. By contrast, isolated nutrients and supplements, a specific geroprotective effect of intermittent fasting, and the clinical utility of epigenetic aging clocks remain unproven. Randomized caloric restriction slows the epigenetic pace of aging only modestly and has so far not demonstrated mortality benefit in humans. title: Goals, motives, and methods of partner influence on cigarette smoking within sexual and/or gender minoritized dual-smoking couples: A qualitative study.
abstract: Introduction Couples wherein both members smoke cigarettes are highly prevalent and unlikely to achieve abstinence. It is known that romantic partners influence one another's smoking behaviors, but little is known about how, why, and to what end. Moreover, few studies have focused on relationships and smoking among marginalized groups despite disproportionate representation of marginalized identities among people who smoke. This qualitative study aimed to characterize attempts to influence partner smoking behaviors within sexual and/or gender minoritized (SGM) dual-smoking couples (DSCs). Methods SGM individuals in a DSC (N=28) were recruited nationally in the United States in 2025. Participants completed a 60-minute semi-structured in-depth interview regarding their relationship's dynamics around smoking and cessation. Analysis followed a team-based, deductive-inductive thematic approach to characterize partners' goals, motives, and methods of attempts to influence smoking and cessation behavior. Results Goals of influencing partner smoking ranged from reducing or stopping to maintaining or increasing smoking. Motives related to health (e.g., partner longevity), finances (e.g., cost of cigarettes), and/or relationship functioning (e.g., avoiding conflict). Methods of influence were verbal (e.g., self-distancing), behavioral (e.g., employing joint strategies), and strategic inaction (e.g., normalizing non-discussion of cessation). summary_short: Introduction Couples wherein both members smoke cigarettes are highly prevalent and unlikely to achieve abstinence. It is known that romantic partners influence one another's smoking behaviors, but little is known about how, why, and to what end.

title: LACA: a cross-species single-cell resource for exploring longevity and aging-associated cellular and molecular programs.
abstract: Different species can have various maximum lifespans, some with exceptional longevity, yet the underlying cellular and molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Despite rapid advances in single-cell transcriptomics, resources that systematically connect single-cell gene expression profiles to species lifespan are limited. We hereby present the Longevity & Aging Cell Atlas (LACA), a database that integrates single-cell transcriptomic datasets across 134 species with their maximum lifespans. LACA includes over 148 million cells with 190 annotated cell types from single-cell datasets. LACA also has a cross-species analytical toolbox of longevity gene comparison, gene-lifespan correlation, and cell-lifespan correlation. These tools allow researchers to better interpret both evolutionarily conserved longevity mechanisms and the evolution of species-specific adaptations in longevity mechanisms without extensive computational expertise. LACA also provides a centenarian single-cell atlas and a human immune aging multi-omics atlas, demonstrating the analytical capability of the resource, as well as 11 different modules for longevity-related analysis, an integrated knowledge graph including curated longevity knowledge bases, and a retrieval-augmented research agent to further facilitate functional interpretation. The database is freely available at https://www.longevityaging.net/ or http://8.142.154.29/LACA/.

title: Incremental associations of pharmacological components in heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction: a systematic review and component network meta-analysis.
abstract: We conducted a component network meta-analysis (CNMA) of phase 3/4 randomized trials to evaluate incremental effects of pharmacological therapies in heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction (HFmrEF/HFpEF; LVEF > 40%). MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane were searched through 1 August 2025 (updated 30 March 2026). We performed an additive CNMA evaluating cardiovascular death or first heart failure hospitalization (HFH) and assessed certainty of evidence. Twenty-four trials and five secondary reports were included. The primary network was sparse (10 trials, 12 regimens), constraining interaction detection and component stability. Incretin-based interventions (pooling semaglutide and tirzepatide, iHR 0.69, 95% CI 0.53-0.91), SGLT-2 inhibitors (0.80, 0.74-0.88), ARNis (0.82, 0.68-0.99), and MRAs (0.89, 0.81-0.98) showed significant component associations, driven principally by fewer HFHs. No drug class significantly reduced mortality. SGLT-2 inhibitors and MRAs remained significant across sensitivity analyses except LVEF ≥ 50%, with SGLT-2 inhibitors most precise. ARNi benefits lost significance under stricter background therapy thresholds (>60%) and contemporary trial restrictions. Evidence for incretins was low-certainty and sensitive to trial selection. SGLT-2 inhibitors and MRAs provide the most robust incremental benefit, while evidence for other drug classes remains context-dependent. No drug class significantly reduced mortality.

title: Skeletal and metabolic effects of anti-sclerostin antibody therapy after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass in an obese ovariectomized mice.
abstract: Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) provides long-term metabolic benefits but accelerates bone loss, particularly in postmenopausal individuals. Circulating sclerostin levels have been reported to increase after RYGB in postmenopausal women, suggesting that sclerostin inhibition may mitigate post-surgical skeletal deterioration. To determine whether anti-sclerostin antibody (Scl-Ab) therapy improves skeletal and metabolic outcomes following RYGB in an obese, ovariectomized (OVX) murine model. Female C57BL/6 J mice were fed a high-fat diet to induce obesity, underwent OVX, and were assigned to RYGB or weight-matched sham surgery. Mice received Scl-Ab or saline for eight weeks. Skeletal outcomes were assessed by three-point bending, micro-computed tomography, histology, and histomorphometry. Metabolic outcomes included glucose tolerance, insulin sensitivity, multiplex hormone profiling, and evaluation of the regulation of sclerostin by glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) in primary periosteal cells. In RYGB mice, Scl-Ab improved femoral biomechanical properties and trabecular bone architecture, increasing trabecular bone area and thickness. It also enhanced glucose tolerance, insulin sensitivity, and circulating GLP-1, gastric inhibitory peptide, and secretin levels. In contrast, Scl-Ab further increased RYGB-associated cortical porosity, highlighting divergent effects on trabecular and cortical bone. title: Laundered Survival: When Target Trial Emulation Doesn't Emulate-Implications for GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Cancer Outcomes.
abstract: Target trial emulation (TTE) is increasingly invoked in observational studies to address time-related biases. Recent observational studies reporting large protective associations between glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and cancer outcomes have cited TTE as a methodological strength. TTE validity, however, depends on explicit alignment of eligibility, treatment assignment, and time zero when outcome start to be counted (EAT0). We conducted a conceptual and quantitative evaluation of two recent observational studies that defined GLP-1 RA exposure using post-baseline information (≥2 prescriptions) while initiating follow-up at the first prescription. We reproduced these designs using Monte Carlo simulation (500 replications; n = 5,000 per replication) under a null treatment effect (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.0), varying the interval between first and second prescriptions. Analyses enforcing EAT0 alignment were used as comparators. By deferring treatment assignment while accruing person-time from an earlier index date, these designs violate a core requirement of TTE. This structure induces immortal time bias through both exposure misclassification and survivor selection. Simulated analyses reproducing these features generated HRs ranging from 0.72 to 0.39 in longer follow-up settings and from 0.85 to 0.60 in shorter follow-up settings, closely approximating published estimates. Recent observational studies reporting large protective associations between glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and cancer outcomes have cited TTE as a methodological strength.

title: Cancer risk with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists: An umbrella review of meta-analyses.
abstract: Use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) for diabetes and obesity is increasing, but effects on uncommon or long-latency cancers are uncertain. We synthesised meta-analytic evidence for overall and site-specific cancer risk and assessed methodological quality, overlap, outcome-level certainty, and credibility. We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception to 30 June 2026 for meta-analyses of GLP-1RAs or the dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide and incident cancer. Randomised and observational evidence was considered separately; review-level estimates were not recombined. We assessed methodological confidence with AMSTAR 2, overlap with corrected covered area (CCA), outcome-level certainty with a GRADE-informed algorithm, and association credibility with Ioannidis criteria. We included 38 meta-analyses from 2012 to 2026. The most comprehensive placebo-controlled randomised evidence (48 trials, 94 245 participants, median follow-up 70 weeks) showed no statistically significant association with thyroid cancer (odds ratio [OR] 1·37, 95% CI 0·82-2·31; 1 fewer to 9 more cases per 10 000 treated), pancreatic cancer (0·84, 0·53-1·35), colorectal cancer (1·11, 0·75-1·65), or breast cancer (0·95, 0·60-1·49), and no overall cancer increase (OR 1·05, 0·98-1·13 across 50 trials). Thyroid and agent-specific haematological signals were inconsistent or based on sparse events; between-review discordance for thyroid and colorectal cancer was larg

title: Where patients obtain GLP-1 receptor agonists: direct-to-consumer channels, compounded product use, and reason-specific nonadherence in a national survey.
abstract: To examine acquisition channels for glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and associations with compounded use, prescription status, and nonadherence. This cross-sectional analysis used the National Center for Health Statistics Rapid Surveys System Round 7 (July-August 2025; N = 8118). Among 976 past-year users, channels were classified as clinician/pharmacy without direct-to-consumer (DTC) acquisition, any DTC telehealth/medical spa, or other. Survey-weighted logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs). GLP-1 RA use was reported by 9.8% of adults, approximately 25.9 million. Of users, 18.3% used a DTC or medical spa channel and 9.2% reported no clinician prescription. Among users reporting known compounded status, compounded use was 73.0% (95% CI, 62.7%-81.2%) for DTC versus 12.9% (8.8%-18.4%) for conventional acquisition (aOR, 14.56; 95% CI, 7.99-26.54). Overall, 22.6% reported compounded use and 8.6% did not know. DTC acquisition was associated with cost-attributed nonadherence (aOR, 4.94; 95% CI, 2.77-8.81); the supply-attributed association was not statistically significant (aOR, 1.15; 95% CI, 0.56-2.38; contrast P < 0.001). Associations were also observed for side-effect-attributed reduction/discontinuation (aOR, 2.12; 95% CI, 1.05-4.27) and complete discontinuation (aOR, 1.83; 95% CI, 1.01-3.32). Counseling associations were imprecise. Insurance nonpayment was associated with DTC acquisition (aOR, 8.01; 95% CI, 4.70-13.67). DTC acquisition
summary_short: DTC acquisition was associated with cost-attributed nonadherence (aOR, 4.94; 95% CI, 2.77-8.81); the supply-attributed association was not statistically significant (aOR, 1.15; 95% CI, 0.56-2.38; contrast P < 0.001). Insurance nonpayment was associated with DTC acquisition (aOR, 8.01; 95% CI, 4.70-13.67).

Advanced Medical Therapeutic Approaches to Treat Chronic Coronary Syndromes: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Chronic coronary syndromes (CCSs) encompass obstructive and non-obstructive coronary artery disease, including epicardial atherosclerosis, coronary microvascular dysfunction, and coronary vasospasm, which may lead to angina pectoris, myocardial infarction, heart attack, and sudden death. Understanding the pathophysiology of CCS has led to targeted therapeutic approaches aimed at managing dyslipidemia, inflammation, and thrombus formation to reduce cardiovascular burden and mortality risk. This review aimed to explore advanced and emerging therapeutic strategies for the treatment of CCS, including advanced lipid-lowering therapies, Lp(a)-lowering RNA agents, novel anti-inflammatory agents, including interleukin-6 (IL-6)-targeted therapy, Factor XIa-targeted antithrombotic therapy, cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibitors (CETP), angiopoietin-like protein 3 (ANGPTL3) inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), nanoparticle-based targeted therapies, and microbiome-modifying therapies. This review situates each therapeutic agent within the 2024 ESC and 2023 ACC/AHA chronic coronary syndrome guidelines and, because regulatory approval, guideline recommendations, and cardiovascular outcome evidence are distinct concepts, considers each separately: high-intensity statins, ezetimibe, PCSK9 inhibitors, low-dose colchicine, and semaglutide are approved and guideline-recommended for defined populations with outcome-trial support; inclisiran and bempedoic acid

title: Real-World Weight Changes of Prescribed Semaglutide Medications and Application of a Novel Cognitive-Behavioral Protocol: A Nonrandomized 12-Month Retrospective Assessment of Women With Obesity.
abstract: Introduction A plethora of data are available on the unsatisfactory outcomes of obesity treatments focused on controlling eating and increasing exercise/physical activity. As a result, there has been an increase in the prescription of semaglutide medications for weight loss. Although 12-month weight reductions associated with such pharmacologic treatments are reported to range from 12% to 18% within controlled settings, lesser reductions are indicated under "real-word" conditions, where treatment compliance is, overall, less favorable. Prior research has also indicated that an evolving cognitive-behavioral obesity treatment that focuses on exercise-related psychological changes carrying over to changes in eating behaviors within real-world settings might improve the weight-loss effects associated with previous behavioral means. Objective The aims of this work were to position future research and generate hypotheses relating to such treatment modalities, especially under randomized conditions. Methods Real-world weight-change data from women with obesity associated with treatments using semaglutide (n = 314) or theory-based cognitive-behavioral processes focused on enhancing self-regulation, initially through increased exercise (n = 95), were measured from baseline to month 12. Results Under the present nonrandomized conditions, the novel cognitive-behavioral treatment was associated with significantly greater weight loss (mean = -6.63 kg, standard deviation = 4.97; -7.0%) tha

title: Natural Products Targeting Metabolic Disorders in Diabetic Kidney Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives.
abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a major microvascular complication of diabetes. Although the emergence of new therapies such as SGLT2 inhibitors, GLP-1 receptor agonists, aldosterone receptor antagonists, and endothelin receptor antagonists (ERAs) has expanded the therapeutic options for DKD, these therapies remain insufficient to meet the urgent clinical needs of contemporary society. Recent studies indicate that the pathogenesis of DKD involves multiple signaling pathways and drug targets. DKD is closely linked to the dysregulation of glucose, lipid, and amino acid metabolism. Compared to synthetic drugs, natural products offer advantages such as broader biological activities, favorable drug-like potential, multi-target mechanisms of action, enhanced safety and tolerability profiles, as well as abundant and renewable sources. Over the past two decades, natural products have demonstrated considerable potential in preclinical DKD studies (triptolide, quercetin, berberine, baicalin, resveratrol, proanthocyanidin B2), and various natural compounds are now considered integral components of comprehensive DKD management strategies, despite their disadvantages of poor solubility and low bioavailability. This review focuses on the cellular and molecular mechanisms through which natural products alleviate DKD by targeting metabolic disorders, summarizes the contributions of nanodelivery systems in improving the bioavailability of natural products, and presents related challenges in
summary_short: Recent studies indicate that the pathogenesis of DKD involves multiple signaling pathways and drug targets.

title: Glucagon-like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists Versus Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 Inhibitors in Heart Transplant Recipients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis.
abstract: Background Heart transplant (HT) recipients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) face elevated risks of cardiac allograft vasculopathy (CAV), rejection, and cardiovascular events. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) confer cardiorenal protection in general T2DM patients, but data specific to HT recipients are scarce. Methods We conducted a retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Adult HT recipients with T2DM who initiated a GLP-1 RA or a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor after transplantation between January 1, 2016, and December 31, 2025, were matched 1:1 on 36 covariates. The primary outcome was a 3-year graft-specific composite of CAV (T86.290), HT rejection (T86.21), or HT failure (T86.22). All-cause mortality and myocardial infarction (I21) or ischemic stroke (I63) were analyzed separately. Results After matching, 712 patients per group were analyzed. At 3 y, the graft-specific composite occurred in 12.1% of GLP-1 RA recipients versus 29.2% of DPP-4 inhibitor recipients (risk ratio [RR] 0.416; 95% confidence interval, 0.299-0.579; P Conclusions In this multicenter electronic health record-based cohort, GLP-1 RA use was associated with lower graft-specific outcomes and all-cause mortality than DPP-4 inhibitor use. CAV did not differ significantly. These observational findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.

title: A novel role of NOX2 in enhancing HBV replication through ROS‑mediated autophagy activation.
abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is a serious global public health issue. Mounting evidence suggests that NADPH oxidase 2 (NOX2) plays critical roles in various physiological and pathological processes. However, the underlying mechanisms by which NOX2 affects HBV infection remain to be elucidated. In the present study, the potential role of NOX2 in HBV replication was investigated in cell models. First, it was demonstrated that NOX2 is highly expressed in transiently and stably HBV‑infected cells. Second, by employing inhibitor, RNA interference technique and plasmid overexpression, it was revealed that NOX2 plays an essential role in promoting HBV replication. Furthermore, the underlying mechanism of how NOX2 affects HBV replication was illustrated. It was found that NOX2‑mediated ROS induce an increase of intracellular autophagy levels, which result in facilitating HBV replication. These results suggested a previously unrecognized role of NOX2 in HBV replication. Taken together, NOX2 may serve as a novel target for developing treatment strategies against HBV‑related disorders.
summary_short: Mounting evidence suggests that NADPH oxidase 2 (NOX2) plays critical roles in various physiological and pathological processes. It was found that NOX2‑mediated ROS induce an increase of intracellular autophagy levels, which result in facilitating HBV replication.

Dissipation of lysosome pH impairs formation and collapses existing LPS-induced lysosome tubules in macrophages.
abstract: While lysosomes are typically globular in morphology, lipopolysaccharide-activated macrophages reorganize lysosomes into an expanded tubular network. Here, we sought to determine if the V-ATPase and the lysosomal pH contribute to LPS-mediated lysosome tubulation in macrophages. We found that inhibition of the V-ATPase prevented lysosome tubulation and collapsed preformed tubules. However, the V-ATPase also controls mTORC1 activity, which itself is needed for tubulation. To distinguish between lysosomal pH and mTORC1, we turned to NH 4 Cl, which alkalinized lysosomal pH but did not interfere with mTORC1; yet NH 4 Cl blocked tubulation, showing that an acidic lysosomal pH is needed for lysosome remodelling. Moreover, clamping the pH to either acidic or alkaline pH caused tubules to collapse, indicating that the pH gradient promotes tubulation, rather than a specific pH. These effects were not due to altered microtubule organization or impaired lysosome motility, suggesting that motors remained associated with lysosomes. On the other hand, while LPS did not alter the average pH of spherical or tubular lysosomes, growing tubules displayed a more acidic peripheral end relative to the pericentral end. Based on this observation, we propose that a localized pH gradient along the tubule may enable tubulation by modulating factors that catalyse tubule growth.
summary_short: We found that inhibition of the V-ATPase prevented lysosome tubulation and collapsed preformed tubules. These effects were not due to altered microtubule organization or impaired lysosome motility, suggesting that motors remained associated with lysosomes.

title: ATP and α-ketoglutarate link nitrogen availability to TORC1-Npr1 signaling in yeast.
abstract: The TORC1 (Target of Rapamycin Complex 1) kinase complex coordinates eukaryotic cell growth and metabolism in response to nutrient availability. In yeast, one of the proteins under TORC1 control is the Npr1 kinase mediating nitrogen control of several plasma membrane transporters, yet the metabolic signals governing this pathway remain poorly understood. Here, we first investigated the previously described and unexpected activation of TORC1-Npr1 signaling upon acute glucose starvation. We show that this response occurs only under specific nitrogen conditions, notably in cells grown on proline or glutamine, and depends on increased ATP production driven by stimulated respiration. In proline-grown cells, this respiration is fueled by catabolism of α-ketoglutarate, while high α-ketoglutarate levels negatively affect TORC1-Npr1 activation. We next analyzed TORC1-Npr1 activation following NH 4 + addition to proline-grown cells. Our results confirm that glutamine accumulation is not required for this activation and instead show that NH 4 + assimilation is associated with a decrease in α-ketoglutarate levels and a sustained increase in ATP production, concomitant with TORC1-Npr1 activation. In cells lacking the NH 4 + -assimilating glutamate dehydrogenases, both increased ATP production and TORC1-Npr1 activation are impaired. Together, these findings identify ATP and α-ketoglutarate as important metabolic determinants of TORC1-Npr1 signaling in response to nitrogen availability.

title: AKT as a central node integrating multidrug resistance mechanisms in ovarian Cancer.
abstract: Ovarian cancer, particularly high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC), remains a leading cause of gynecologic cancer mortality. Although HGSOC responds to platinum-taxane therapy, 70-85% relapse, with acquired resistance playing a major role. The phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (AKT)/mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway, centered on AKT, contributes to this resistance. Current literature examines AKT's downstream consequences in isolation, overlooking their collective contribution to tumor evolution; this review addresses that gap by separating upstream AKT activation from downstream resistance outputs. Intrinsic genomic alterations (PIK3CA mutation, phosphatase and tensin homolog [PTEN] loss) and extrinsic tumor microenvironment (TME) cues converge on AKT, which drives four emerging resistance mechanisms (metabolic reprogramming and ferroptosis evasion, epigenetic modulation of homologous recombination inhibitor sensitivity, cancer stem cell plasticity, and immune evasion, discussed with therapeutic targeting), integrated with classical mechanisms into a unified chemoresistance framework. AKT promotes chemoresistance by coordinating ATP-binding cassette transporter-mediated drug efflux, RAD51/BRCA-dependent DNA repair, and an elevated apoptotic threshold via Bcl-2-associated agonist of cell death and survivin modulation. Spatial organization and interconnections are highlighted, including amplified AKT activation at the tumor-stromal interface throu
summary_short: Ovarian cancer, particularly high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC), remains a leading cause of gynecologic cancer mortality. Although HGSOC responds to platinum-taxane therapy, 70-85% relapse, with acquired resistance playing a major role.

title: Dietary alanyl-glutamine modulates glutamine metabolism, mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) signaling and metabolic homeostasis in juvenile mud crab (Scylla paramamosain).
abstract: The mechanisms by which alanyl-glutamine (Ala-Gln) may affect growth and intestinal function in juvenile mud crab remain insufficiently understood. To address this gap, this study evaluated growth, nutrient metabolism, and intestinal health in juvenile mud crab (Scylla paramamosain). A total of 108 crabs (5.91 ± 0.22 g) received three isonitrogenous and isolipidic diets containing 0%, 1% or 2% supplemental Ala-Gln for 9 weeks. Both supplementation levels improved growth, feed utilization and muscle protein content, without significant differences between them. Supplementation increased hepatopancreatic glutamine and glutamate concentrations and glutaminase and glutamate dehydrogenase activities. These responses were accompanied by enhanced mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) signaling, reduced hepatopancreatic lipid accumulation, and increased glycogen and pyruvate contents. Intestinal morphology improved at 2%, alongside changes in apoptosis-related and barrier-associated gene and protein expression. Overall, Ala-Gln supplementation improved growth and feed utilization in association with changes in glutamine metabolism, mTOR-related signaling and intestinal characteristics. Increasing supplementation from 1% to 2% did not consistently provide additional benefits, and an optimal supplementation level remains undetermined. The absence of an equimolar free alanine-glutamine control precludes attribution of the observed benefits specifically to the dipeptide form.
summary_short: Intestinal morphology improved at 2%, alongside changes in apoptosis-related and barrier-associated gene and protein expression. Overall, Ala-Gln supplementation improved growth and feed utilization in association with changes in glutamine metabolism, mTOR-related signaling and intestinal characteristics.

title: Age-Stratified Sirolimus Trough Concentrations in Pediatric Vascular Malformations: A Real-World Retrospective Study.
abstract: Background Sirolimus is increasingly being used off-label to treat pediatric vascular malformations. In this study, the age-stratified drug exposure, pharmacokinetic variability, and long-term treatment characteristics of sirolimus were evaluated in a real-world pediatric population. Methods In this study, 144 patients (younger than 19 years) with vascular malformations who were treated with sirolimus at a single center (July 2018 and March 2025) were retrospectively analyzed. A total of 2054 therapeutic drug monitoring measurements were obtained. The patients were stratified into 6 age groups (1 month and younger to 12-18 years). The outcomes included trough concentration, interindividual variability (coefficient of variation), target range attainment, treatment duration, and MRI-based response. Results The median follow-up was 18.3 months (range, 0.3-74.1 months). Neonates (1 month and younger) showed the highest interindividual variability (coefficient of variation = 61.6%), with lower variability observed in adolescents (40.0%, P 15 ng/mL) were most frequent in neonates (6.6%). Prolonged therapy (≥24 months) was observed in 31.9% of patients, with a median duration of 35.1 months. Among the 44 patients who underwent follow-up MRI, 84.1% showed disease improvement or stability. Conclusions Sustained long-term treatment continuity suggests that sirolimus was generally tolerated across pediatric age groups, although direct toxicity data were not systematically captured in th

title: Target of rapamycin and regulation of membrane transporters: integrating nutrient sensing, stress adaptation and lifespan across eukaryotes.
abstract: Nutrient availability is typically treated as an input to the target of rapamycin (TOR) pathway, the conserved controller of growth, metabolism and ageing. Yet, membrane transporters are not merely suppliers of the amino acids and other nutrients that activate TOR, they are integral components of the signalling network itself, and TOR in turn governs their activity, abundance, trafficking and degradation. This bidirectional coupling - including transporters that double as receptors, or 'transceptors' - is mechanistically defined in budding yeast, where the TORC1 complex acts through the Npr1-arrestin axis and vacuolar Gtr/EGO amino acid sensing, conserved in fission yeast, where TOR links nitrogen transport and vacuolar function to growth, stress and lifespan; and elaborated in metazoans across intestinal and fat-body uptake, endocrine relays and lysosomal gatekeepers such as SLC38A9, NPC1 and TRPML1. We propose that TOR-transporter coupling offers a conserved and mechanistically compelling, but still, largely untested, route linking nutrient transport to stress resistance and lifespan across eukaryotes and we advance it as a framework to guide future causal work rather than a settled conclusion.

title: Mitochondrial dysfunction in T‑cell exhaustion: Its contribution to the efficacy of cancer immunotherapy (Review).
abstract: Mitochondria play a pivotal role in the regulation of T‑cell function, particularly in the context of T‑cell exhaustion within the tumor microenvironment. T‑cell exhaustion, characterized by impaired effector functions and the sustained expression of inhibitory receptors, poses a significant barrier to effective antitumor immunity and limits the success of immunotherapies. Emerging evidence indicates that mitochondrial dysfunction is a contributor to the metabolic and functional decline of tumor‑infiltrating lymphocytes. The present review critically synthesizes the available mechanistic and translational literature on mitochondrial dysfunction in T‑cell exhaustion, with particular attention paid to mitochondrial dynamics, mitophagy, and the threshold‑dependent duality of mitochondrial reactive oxygen species. The evidence is organized not by pathway alone, but by intervention class and level of evidence, so that the strategies with demonstrated clinical traction can be distinguished from those that remain at the proof‑of‑concept stage. Of note, four intervention classes are discussed: Metabolic reprogramming, enhancement of mitochondrial biogenesis, redox‑directed modulation and intercellular mitochondrial transfer, together with mitochondria‑directed pharmacological and nanoscale delivery platforms. Clinical translation is assessed against trials registered on ClinicalTrials.gov, of which the most advanced evaluate metformin in combination with immune checkpoint inhibitors.
summary_short: Emerging evidence indicates that mitochondrial dysfunction is a contributor to the metabolic and functional decline of tumor‑infiltrating lymphocytes.

title: Metformin mitigates trophoblast GLUT1 inhibition through HIF-1α/Fibronectin/AMPK pathway in preeclampsia.
abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a complex gestational hypertensive disorder associated with dysregulated placental energy metabolism, and fibronectin (FN) plays a critical role in its development. Although metformin has shown potential in reducing the risk of PE, its effects on FN and trophoblast glucose transport regulation remain unclear. In this study, experiments were conducted using FN-pretreated and FN-knockdown HTR-8/SVneo cells, clinical placental specimens, and a preeclampsia mouse model. Aberrant FN and GLUT1 expression was observed in human preeclamptic placentas. Under hypoxic conditions, FN and GLUT1 were upregulated in two trophoblastic cell lines (HTR-8/SVneo and JAR) and in primary placental cells. However, exogenous FN suppressed hypoxia-associated GLUT1 upregulation, reduced extracellular L-lactate levels, and impaired trophoblast invasion and ciliogenesis. These effects were associated with activation of AMPK signaling. Metformin reduced HIF-1α, FN, and phosphorylated AMPK levels in FN-treated trophoblasts under hypoxia, while increasing GLUT1 expression and extracellular L-lactate levels and restoring trophoblast invasion and ciliogenesis. Notably, metformin increased AMPK phosphorylation in FN-silenced cells, suggesting that its effects on AMPK signaling depend, at least partly, on FN status.
