In the mouse model, increased placental FN was accompanied by altered GLUT1 expression, impaired primary cilia formation, and changes in AMPK-related signaling.

title: GnRH-a Plus Letrozole vs Ethinylestradiol/Cyproterone Acetate Plus Metformin in Progestin-Insensitive Endometrial Atypical Hyperplasia: A Multicenter Phase II RCT.
abstract: Effective second-line fertility-preserving treatment for progestin-insensitive endometrial atypical hyperplasia (EAH) has not been established. We compare the efficacy and safety of gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist (GnRH-a) plus letrozole with ethinylestradiol/cyproterone acetate (Diane-35) plus metformin in this population. In this multicenter, open-label, randomized phase II trial, patients aged 18-45 years with progestin-insensitive EAH seeking fertility preservation were assigned 1:1 to GnRH-a plus letrozole or Diane-35 plus metformin. Treatment response was assessed by scheduled hysteroscopy with pathological evaluation. The primary endpoint was the complete response (CR) rate within 28 weeks after second-line treatment initiation. Secondary endpoints reported in this analysis included time to CR, adverse events and compliance. From July 2022 to July 2025, 41 patients were randomized and analyzed by intention-to-treat analysis. CR within 28 weeks was achieved in 19 of 20 patients (95.0%) in the GnRH-a plus letrozole group and 14 of 21 patients (66.7%) in the Diane-35 plus metformin group, corresponding to a risk difference of 28.3 percentage points (95% CI, 3.7-50.0; two-sided Fisher's exact P=0.045). Median time to CR was shorter in the GnRH-a plus letrozole group than in the Diane-35 plus metformin group (12.86 weeks vs. 17.29 weeks, HR, 2.12; 95% CI, 1.05-4.28; log-rank P=0.029). title: Long-term metformin therapy and risk of anemia in type 2 diabetes.
abstract: Metformin is the cornerstone therapy for type 2 diabetes (T2D) and is prescribed long term to large patient populations, making its potential hematological effects clinically relevant. Particular attention has focused on metformin-associated vitamin B12 deficiency and its possible contribution to anemia. Accumulating evidence demonstrates that metformin reduces serum vitamin B12 concentrations and increases the risk of biochemical deficiency, particularly with higher doses and prolonged treatment. However, its overall effects on hemoglobin levels and anemia risk remain modest and variable across clinical populations. Importantly, anemia in patients with T2D is multifactorial and may result from chronic kidney disease, iron deficiency, systemic inflammation, blood loss, or other nutritional deficiencies, complicating the identification of metformin's independent contribution. Although vitamin B12 depletion represents a plausible mechanism linking metformin exposure to hematological abnormalities, additional metabolic and clinical factors may influence erythropoiesis and hemoglobin homeostasis. Furthermore, longer treatment duration and greater cumulative exposure may increase the likelihood of vitamin B12 deficiency, highlighting the importance of appropriate clinical surveillance. Accordingly, this narrative review critically examines the relationship between long-term metformin therapy and anemia risk in patients with T2D, with particular emphasis on vitamin B12 depletion, a
summary_short: Accumulating evidence demonstrates that metformin reduces serum vitamin B12 concentrations and increases the risk of biochemical deficiency, particularly with higher doses and prolonged treatment.

title: Taurine Protects Against Paclitaxel-Induced Testicular Injury in Adult Rats by Mitigating Oxidative Stress and Apoptotic Cell Death.
abstract: To evaluate the protective effects of taurine against paclitaxel-induced testicular, hormonal, metabolic, and molecular alterations in male rats. Adult male rats were randomly allocated into four groups (n = 8 per group): control, taurine alone (150mg/kg/day), paclitaxel alone (2mg/kg every other day), and paclitaxel plus taurine. Sperm parameters, serum reproductive hormones (testosterone, FSH, and LH), and metabolic markers (glucose and cholesterol) were measured. Testicular oxidative stress was evaluated by determining malondialdehyde (MDA), superoxide dismutase (SOD), and glutathione peroxidase (GSH-Px) levels. At the same time, the inflammatory status was assessed by measuring tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) and interleukin-1β (IL-1β). In addition, the mRNA expression levels of apoptosis-related genes (BCL-2 and P53) and the steroidogenic gene STAR were quantified by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR). Testicular histopathological changes were assessed using the Johnsen scoring system. Paclitaxel reduced sperm motility by 57.7%, increased abnormal forms by 188%, and lowered epididymal sperm number by 42.9% and testosterone by 54.1%. title: Epigenetic programming of immune cells: unleashing anti-tumor potential and clinical perspectives.
abstract: Immune cell plasticity is a defining feature of tumor immunity and is increasingly recognized as being governed by epigenetic regulation. Advances in single-cell and spatial multi-omics have uncovered an epigenetic checkpoint that integrates environmental cues within the tumor microenvironment (TME) to shape immune cell fate and function. In this review, we synthesize recent evidence supporting three interconnected paradigms of epigenetic control in tumor immunity from the perspective of immune cell heterogeneity, ecology, and state transitions. First, dynamic chromatin remodeling programs myeloid cell polarization and functional diversification. Second, epitranscriptomic regulation constrains T and B cell states, contributing to immune dysfunction and exhaustion. Third, spatially resolved epigenetic remodeling influences immune cell trafficking, positioning, and retention within tumors. Collectively, these mechanisms establish durable immune states that reinforce TME-driven immunosuppression. We further highlight emerging pharmacological strategies targeting epigenetic regulators to reprogram immune cell function and enhance anti-tumor immunity. This framework provides a foundation for leveraging epigenetic plasticity to improve the efficacy of cancer immunotherapy.
summary_short: Immune cell plasticity is a defining feature of tumor immunity and is increasingly recognized as being governed by epigenetic regulation. title: Calcium-porphyrin metal organic framework/starch hybrid beads for pH-responsive and photostable drug delivery of Nifuroxazide and Omeprazole.
abstract: Drug-loaded beads have attracted significant interest as advanced delivery systems due to their ability to enhance drug stability, bioavailability, and controlled release. Omeprazole and Nifuroxazide suffer from challenges such as acid degradation, poor dissolution, and limited stability, which can reduce their therapeutic effectiveness. Encapsulation within bead-based carriers protects these drugs from gastrointestinal conditions and enables targeted release, thereby improving their overall therapeutic performance. To overcome these drawbacks, this work has engineered a novel oral drug delivery system in the form of a Ca-TCPP/starch bead. This innovative platform leverages the porous structure of the Ca-TCPP material to achieve substantial drug encapsulation and high loading capabilities. In this study, a calcium-tetrakis(4-carboxyphenyl)porphyrin (Ca-TCPP) MOF was successfully synthesized and incorporated into starch-based spherical beads to construct a hybrid inorganic-organic carrier with improved structural stability and controlled release behaviour. Comprehensive characterization using FT-IR, PXRD, SEM, EDX, and BET analyses confirmed the formation of a mesoporous composite featuring uniformly dispersed nanocrystalline MOF domains within the biopolymeric matrix. The Ca-TCPP@starch beads were evaluated as drug delivery vehicles for Nifuroxazide and omeprazole. Both drugs exhibit stability limitations under physiological conditions. title: How I Do It: pearls and pitfalls in open preperitoneal ventral hernia repair.
abstract: Background The open preperitoneal ventral hernia repair (OPPVHR) permits wide mesh overlap in an extraperitoneal space without the need for a myofascial release. This operation has a distinct learning curve, which once overcome, can be widely applied to a variety of hernia types. Objective To provide surgeons new to OPPVHR with a practical, step-by-step reference of pearls and pitfalls that support operative success and reproducible outcomes. Results Drawing on institutional experience and the supporting literature, the authors outline eleven thematic principles spanning the perioperative continuum from preoperative optimization, through practical and evidence-based surgical techniques and finally, management of skin and subcutaneous tissues and postoperative care. The pearls and pitfalls that are presented are supported by quality-improvement data from institutional experience. Conclusions OPPVHR offers durable repair of complex ventral hernias and has a number of distinct advantages compared to alternative techniques. Its success depends on identifying the correct plane, achieving fascial closure, and ensuring adequate mesh coverage while avoiding the distinct error traps present at each operative step. A thorough understanding of abdominal wall anatomy, careful patient selection, and disciplined adherence to sound operative principles remain the cornerstones of a successful repair.
summary_short: Background The open preperitoneal ventral hernia repair (OPPVHR) permits wide mesh overlap in an extraperitoneal space without the need for a myofascial release. This operation has a distinct learning curve, which once overcome, can be widely applied to a variety of hernia types.

title: Expert consensus on periodontal management for medically compromised patients.
abstract: Periodontitis is a highly prevalent oral disease that extends beyond local inflammation and tissue destruction to exert a profound influence on systemic health. With the growing burden of multimorbidity, where multiple systemic disorders frequently co-exist, periodontal management has become increasingly complex, yet clear and integrated guidance for this specific patient population remains limited. This manuscript synthesizes current evidence on the bidirectional relationship between periodontitis and systemic conditions, proposes recommendations for dynamic periodontal management, and updates relevant therapeutic strategies. This expert consensus is designed to ensure both the safety and efficacy of periodontal treatment, reduce the risk of complications, and ultimately promote oral and general well-being.

Dumping syndrome alleviated with semaglutide in a patient with hypoglycemia refractory to standard therapy.
abstract: Dumping syndrome after Nissen fundoplication is uncommon with therapeutic challenges. Accelerated gastric transit and dysregulated incretin-mediated insulin secretion are believed to drive postprandial hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia. Treatment frequently fails to achieve sustained symptom control and is constrained by adverse effects. This case describes glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist therapy as a novel approach to address glycemic instability and gastrointestinal symptoms. A 55-year-old man presented with a 10-year history of persistent gastrointestinal distress and postprandial hypoglycemia, including irritability, fatigue, and cognitive impairment after Nissen fundoplication. After hospitalization to rule out insulinoma, outpatient follow-up led to a diagnosis of dumping syndrome with severe hypoglycemia. He was initiated on semaglutide. There was a decline in the frequency of hypoglycemia, with improvement in gastrointestinal symptoms, glycemic stabilization, and quality of life. This highlights the utility of off-label GLP-1 receptor agonists in patients with dumping syndrome, resulting in a reduction in postprandial hypoglycemic episodes. Although emerging reports have described similar benefits, evidence remains limited. Further studies are needed to clarify efficacy, safety, and appropriate patient selection before GLP-1-based therapies can be recommended for dumping syndrome.
summary_short: Dumping syndrome after Nissen fundoplication is uncommon with therapeutic challenges. Accelerated gastric transit and dysregulated incretin-mediated insulin secretion are believed to drive postprandial hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia.

title: Risk of infectious spondylitis after tirzepatide versus semaglutide initiation in adults with type 2 diabetes: A multinational real-world active-comparator cohort study.
abstract: Infectious spondylitis is a rare but clinically severe infection to which type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) predisposes. Although incretin-based therapies may influence inflammatory and infection-related pathways, comparative evidence on serious site-specific infections after tirzepatide versus semaglutide initiation remains limited. This study compared the 365-day risk of coded infectious spondylitis between adults with T2DM who started tirzepatide and those who started semaglutide. This active-comparator, new-user cohort study drew on the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network and included adults with T2DM who started tirzepatide or semaglutide between July 1, 2022, and March 25, 2026. We excluded patients with any recorded use of a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist or tirzepatide before the index date and those with a history of spinal infection. Groups were matched 1:1 on propensity scores incorporating demographic, metabolic, comorbidity, medication, infection-related, substance-use, and spine-procedure variables. The primary outcome was coded infectious spondylitis (ICD-10-CM M46.2, M46.3, or G06.1 recorded as a primary or secondary diagnosis) on days 1-365. Sensitivity analyses evaluated alternative outcome definitions, baseline covariates, initiation periods, follow-up maturity, and 730-day follow-up. title: Substance-related and psychiatric outcomes associated with GLP-1 receptor agonists versus lisdexamfetamine in adults with binge eating disorder: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Binge-eating disorder (BED) is associated with substantial psychiatric burden and elevated substance-related vulnerability. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists(GLP-1RAs) have recently emerged as potentially effective therapeutic options for binge eating disorder(BED). However, real-world evidence comparing GLP-1 RAs with approved lisdexamfetamine(LDX) remains limited. Using the TriNetX US Research Network, we conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults diagnosed with BED between 2010 and 2025 who received GLP-1 RAs or LDX. Primary outcomes were alcohol use disorder(AUD) and substance use disorder(SUD). Secondary outcomes included positive substance and alcohol screening results, suicidal ideation, self-harm behavior, cardiovascular events, and cerebrovascular events. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 2,454 patients remained in each group. Relative risks(RRs) and hazard ratios(HRs) were calculated. After matching, GLP-1 RA use was associated with a lower risk of SUD than LDX (2.4% vs. 3.5%, RR, 0.715;95% confidence interval[CI], 0.513-0.996;p=0.034). For secondary outcomes, compared with LDX, GLP-1 RA use was associated with significantly lower positive substance screening results (4.3%vs. 12.2%; RR, 0.351; 95% CI, 0.280-0.441; p<0.001) and lower risk of suicide ideation (0.8% vs. 1.5%;RR, 0.525; 95% CI,0.298-0.924;p=0.023). title: Detection of Potential Drug-drug Interactions in a Community Pharmacy: A Retrospective Cross-sectional Study Supporting the Role of Community Pharmacists in the Health System.
abstract: Introduction and objectives Drug interactions are a major public health concern because they can compromise patient safety and increase healthcare costs. Community pharmacists play a key role in identifying and preventing these interactions. This study aimed to evaluate the role of community pharmacists in detecting pharmacological interactions by studying detected drug interactions in community pharmacies, their severity, and the medications most commonly involved. Methods A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted in 167 chronic polymedicated patients with electronic prescriptions recruited through a pharmacotherapeutic follow-up service at a community pharmacy in Murcia, Spain. Anonymized data on detected drug interactions were collected over four years using the "Interactions" tool of the Unycop® version 4.8 pharmacy management system. Statistical analyses were performed using RStudio® version 3.6.3. Results A total of 1330 medications and 577 drug interactions were identified. The mean number of interactions per patient was 3.46 (SD = 0.08). The drugs most frequently involved were hydrochlorothiazide, metformin, omeprazole, furosemide, and bisoprolol. Diuretics and antidiabetics were the pharmacological groups most commonly associated with interactions. Severe interactions accounted for 5% of cases, while 40% were moderate. The number of interactions increased significantly with the number of prescribed medications. Discussion The high prevalence of drug interac
summary_short: Diuretics and antidiabetics were the pharmacological groups most commonly associated with interactions. The number of interactions increased significantly with the number of prescribed medications.

title: MOTS-c: A Narrative Review of Cell and Molecular, Preclinical, Clinical, and Regulatory Literature in Regenerative, Longevity, and Pain Medicine.
abstract: MOTS-c (mitochondrial open reading frame of the 12S rRNA type-c) is a 16-amino-acid peptide encoded within the mitochondrial 12S rRNA gene. In vitro studies at the cellular and molecular level have reported four molecular actions. MOTS-c activates AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) indirectly by inhibiting the folate cycle, translocates to the nucleus under metabolic stress, interacts with Raptor, and binds directly to casein kinase 2. Mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and cellular senescence have each been implicated in osteoarthritis, disc degeneration, osteoporosis, and sarcopenia. In animal models, MOTS-c has been reported to reduce particle-induced osteolysis, suppress ovariectomy-induced bone loss, delay cartilage degeneration, attenuate immobilization-induced muscle atrophy, and support plasma membrane repair. Late-life intermittent treatment improved physical performance in aged mice, although the lifespan curve was not statistically significant. Antinociception has been reported across five preclinical rodent pain models, with AMPK dependence tested in four. No dedicated pharmacokinetic or toxicology study of MOTS-c has been published in any species, and the only completed human trial used an engineered analog rather than the peptide sequence itself; a Phase 2a trial of the unmodified sequence began enrolling in 2026 without reported results. title: Mitochondrial Respiratory Capacity of Donor Somatic Cells Correlates with the Phagocytic Function of Human iPSC-Derived Macrophages.
abstract: Human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived macrophages (iMacs) are promising for cell therapy and disease modeling, but functional variability among hiPSC lines hinders standardization. Because phagocytosis depends on mitochondrial fitness, we hypothesized that the mitochondrial respiratory capacity of donor somatic cells would correlate with the phagocytic function of the corresponding iMacs. We measured mitochondrial respiration in somatic cells from four donors, generated hiPSCs from each line, and differentiated them into macrophages under identical conditions. The donor somatic cells showed graded differences in spare respiratory capacity (SRC). All hiPSC lines showed equivalent pluripotency, and the resulting iMacs were indistinguishable in morphology and surface marker expression. Nevertheless, somatic cell SRC correlated with iMac SRC ( R 2 = 0.91), and phagocytic efficiency differed significantly among all iMac lines, following the rank order of donor somatic cell SRC. These findings indicate that the mitochondrial respiratory capacity of donor cells is associated with the functional quality of iMacs. Profiling it before reprogramming may therefore serve as an early screening strategy for selecting donors for macrophage-based cell therapies.
summary_short: These findings indicate that the mitochondrial respiratory capacity of donor cells is associated with the functional quality of iMacs.

title: Heart-to-Muscle Signaling in Heart Failure: Which Catabolic Mediators Are Truly Cardiac-Derived?
abstract: Heart failure (HF) is frequently accompanied by skeletal muscle wasting, which is present in about one in five ambulatory patients and linked to reduced exercise capacity. It is traditionally viewed as secondary to hypoperfusion, inactivity, and inflammation, yet circulating mediators rising with myocardial stress also act on muscle, and some are released by the stressed heart. We examine heart-to-muscle signaling as a directional axis, distinguishing mediators whose circulating pool is demonstrably cardiac from those for which a cardiac contribution to the circulating pool is unproven or unquantified. Across five soluble mediators (growth differentiation factor 15, fibroblast growth factor 21, myostatin, angiotensin II and activin A) and cardiac extracellular vesicles, cardiac-specific loss- and gain-of-function evidence exists only for myostatin; for growth differentiation factor 15 and fibroblast growth factor 21, a dominant cardiac contribution to the circulating pool is unproven, so the axis is better termed cardiac-stress-associated than cardiac-derived. We link each mediator to the muscle phenotype and to therapies in trials, and define the arteriovenous-sampling and cardiac loss-of-function experiments needed before the axis can be considered a validated therapeutic target.
summary_short: Heart failure (HF) is frequently accompanied by skeletal muscle wasting, which is present in about one in five ambulatory patients and linked to reduced exercise capacity.

title: A Multi-Omics and Systems Biology Perspective on the Potential Inverse Association Between Alzheimer's Disease and Glioblastoma: A Hypothesis-Generating Narrative Review.
abstract: Background : Alzheimer's disease (AD) and glioblastoma (GBM) are characterized by opposing cellular phenotypes (neurodegeneration versus uncontrolled proliferation) and have been considered for a long time as unrelated, but have been increasingly studied in the last decade because of their major individual, social, and economic burden. Several recent epidemiological studies reported an inverse association between AD and brain cancers, yet the biological basis of this relationship remains incompletely understood. Objective and Methods : This work aims to synthesise current evidence on the potential inverse relationship between AD and GBM, considering shared molecular pathways and divergent regulatory mechanisms through a multi-omics and systems-biology approach. Results : Multi-omics data reveal that AD and GBM share overlapping molecular pathways related to cell cycle regulation, apoptosis, metabolism, and immune responses, but exhibit opposite patterns of regulation. Transcriptomic analyses suggest inverse gene expression signatures, while proteomic and metabolomic studies highlight contrasting states of protein homeostasis and energy metabolism. Epigenetic modifications further contribute to disease-specific regulatory landscapes. Systems biology approaches identify key hub nodes, such as p53 and the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway, that may act as molecular switches between neurodegeneration and tumorigenesis. title: Current Landscape in Clinical Drug Repurposing: From Non-Oncology Drugs to New Cancer Applications.
abstract: Drug repurposing builds on pharmacological and safety information already available for an approved drug, but this advantage requires additional studies to establish the biological effect and related mechanisms of action. We conducted a clinically focused review of non-oncology drugs tested as active cancer treatments in interventional studies from 1 January 2021 to 31 July 2026. Randomized trials, phase II-III studies, biomarker-selected cohorts, and studies reporting pharmacokinetics or human target engagement were prioritized. Despite the large number of registered studies, the landscape is still dominated by early-phase, academically sponsored trials. Several widely studied candidates, including metformin, nelfinavir, disulfiram-copper, losartan, and propofol, were negative in randomized evaluations. Conversely, aspirin reduced recurrence in localized colorectal cancer with PI3K-pathway alterations, while preoperative peritumoral lidocaine administration was associated with improved disease-free survival and overall survival in a randomized breast cancer trial. Smaller randomized trials investigating pharmacological ascorbate in pancreatic cancer and simvastatin in recurrent small-cell lung cancer provided preliminary efficacy signals that require confirmation in larger studies. summary_short: Conversely, aspirin reduced recurrence in localized colorectal cancer with PI3K-pathway alterations, while preoperative peritumoral lidocaine administration was associated with improved disease-free survival and overall survival in a randomized breast cancer trial.

title: Stage-Specific Fruiting-Body Counts and Associated Molecular and Biochemical Responses of <i>Morchella sextelata</i> Under Nutrient-Bag and Soil Potassium Carbonate Application Regimes.
abstract: Fruiting-body formation and maturation are major determinants of morel production, but their responses to different K 2 CO 3 supplementation regimes remain insufficiently understood. We compared nutrient-bag and soil application regimes in Morchella sextelata by integrating stage-specific fruiting-body counts with transcriptomic, proteomic, co-expression network, and targeted biochemical analyses. Young- and mature-stage fruiting bodies were counted at 77 and 92 days after sowing, respectively. Within the nutrient-bag series (0.27, 2.70, and 27.0 g K 2 CO 3 /m 2 ), the medium-dose treatment produced the highest counts at both observations. Within the soil series (50 and 500 g K 2 CO 3 /m 2 ), the high-dose treatment produced the highest young-stage count but the lowest mature-stage count, whereas the medium-dose treatment produced the highest mature-stage count. Young-stage molecular responses involved carbohydrate metabolism and ubiquinone biosynthesis, and high-dose soil application was accompanied by the highest trehalose and glucose contents. Mature-stage responses involved nitrogen and amino acid metabolism and lipid-related processes. Mature fruiting bodies under medium-dose soil application had the highest glutamine synthetase activity and the highest contents of glutamate, glutamine, linoleic acid, and palmitic acid. title: Comparative Accuracy of a Commercial Multimodal Large Language Model Versus Clinicians in Dental Age and Sex Estimation from Panoramic Radiographs: A Benchmark Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Routine dental imaging captures cumulative dentoalveolar and periodontal changes, offering a non-invasive window into both chronological aging and physiological senescence. While task-specific deep learning models have been widely explored in dental radiology, the zero-shot diagnostic performance of commercial Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in adult populations remains underinvestigated. The aim of this study was to benchmark the zero-shot diagnostic accuracy and repeatability of a commercial MLLM against human clinicians of varying experience levels in estimating adult dental age and biological sex from panoramic radiographs (OPGs), using documented chronological age and biological sex as the ground truth. Methods: From 216 initially screened records, this retrospective single-center study included 127 standardized, anonymized OPGs from patients (74 men, 53 women; mean chronological age 55.5 ± 15.8 years, range 18-90 years) treated at the Clinical Department of Cranio-Maxillofacial Surgery, Military Institute of Medicine-National Research Institute in Warsaw. title: Real-World Twelve-Month Weight Loss Outcomes in a Comprehensive Obesity Care Program Utilizing Individualized Nutrition Therapy and Incretin-Based Obesity Medications.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Incretin-based obesity medications (IOMs) produce substantial weight loss, but the added benefit of structured nutritional therapy remains unclear. We compared 12-month weight loss between individualized carbohydrate-reduced nutritional therapy plus IOMs (VINT + IOM) and IOM-based care without structured nutritional therapy (IOM only). Methods: In this retrospective cohort study of 4269 adults in a telemedicine obesity care program (VINT + IOM, n = 1658; IOM only, n = 2611), both pathways included clinician-guided medication management and behavioral coaching. The primary analysis included GLP-1-naïve participants on a single ingredient (semaglutide or tirzepatide). Adjusted weight change was estimated using longitudinal linear mixed-effects models. Results: Retention through 12 months was 77% (VINT + IOM) vs. 72% (IOM only). In GLP-1-naïve semaglutide users, adjusted 12-month weight loss was greater with VINT + IOM than IOM only (13.9 vs. 10.9 kg; difference 3.0 kg, 95% CI 0.6-5.4; p = 0.012); observed loss was 13.3% vs. 11.1%. In tirzepatide users, adjusted loss was 20.8 vs. 15.6 kg (difference 5.2 kg, 95% CI 1.8-8.7; p = 0.003); observed loss was 19.7% vs. 15.6%. Responder rates favored VINT + IOM. title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Restores Obesity-Induced Impairment of Taste-Guided Appetitive Behaviors Through Striatum Gi Signaling.
abstract: Diet-induced obesity (DIO) influences taste-guided behavior; however, the neural mechanism remains unclear. We investigated how DIO and administration of semaglutide (Sema), a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, affect behavioral responses to basic tastes in mice using a brief-access taste test. The same mice were assessed repeatedly from lean to DIO conditions. Those with DIO selectively exhibited reduced preference for appetitive tastes, including sweet, umami, and fat, whereas their preference for aversive tastes, such as bitter and sour, was largely comparable to those observed when the mice were lean. Sema treatment in DIO mice restored preference toward appetitive tastes. However, this effect was not reproduced by pair-feeding or dietary restriction, indicating that recovery of taste-guided behavior was not solely because of calorie restriction. As DIO decreases cell surface expression of the Gi-coupled dopamine type 2 receptor in the striatum to alter food-related behaviors, we chemogenetically activated Gi-coupled designer receptors exclusively activated by designer drugs (DREADDs). Chemogenetic activation of Gi-DREADD in the striatum restored the reduced sweet taste response even in DIO mice. Thus, Sema reversed impaired preference for appetitive tastes in DIO mice. Specifically, Gi signaling in the striatum may contribute to this restoration.

title: Helodermatid Venom Exendins: Evolutionary Diversification, Receptor Pharmacology, and Biomedical Translation.
abstract: Helodermatid exendins provide a framework for examining how venom peptide diversification relates to receptor recognition and biomedical potential. This narrative review integrates published evolutionary models with sequence, structural, and pharmacological evidence for helospectins, helodermin, and exendins-3 and -4. A complementary maximum-likelihood analysis compares 17 precursor-length records and 18 peptide-core records, distinguishing characterized Heloderma sequences from homology-based predictions. Precursor and signal/propeptide analyses support the exendin-3/exendin-4 pair, while the peptide-core analysis supports the helospectin/helodermin pair, revealing region-dependent sequence relationships. We examine how amino acid substitutions, C-terminal variation, and post-translational modifications relate to interactions with class B1 G protein-coupled receptors. Helospectins exhibit species-dependent receptor preferences, while comparisons between exendin-3 and exendin-4 associate limited N-terminal variation with distinct pharmacological profiles in historical pancreatic assays. These observations connect molecular diversity with experimental pharmacology while keeping sequence relationships distinct from receptor selectivity and biological function. Exendin-4-derived therapeutics and imaging agents illustrate the biomedical development of a venom peptide scaffold. title: Cardiometabolic Multimorbidity in Older Adults: Risk Assessment, Individualised Treatment, and Evidence Gaps.
abstract: Cardiometabolic multimorbidity, encompassing combinations of hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidaemia, obesity, and cardiovascular disease, is highly prevalent in older adults and drives excess mortality, disability, and healthcare utilisation. Yet, older adults-especially those ≥75 years with frailty, multimorbidity, or cognitive impairment-remain underrepresented in pivotal cardiometabolic randomised trials, limiting the applicability of current risk scores, treatment thresholds, and guideline recommendations to geriatric patients. This narrative review synthesises the contemporary evidence on cardiometabolic medicine in older adults, highlighting the gaps in epidemiology, risk stratification, therapeutic decision-making, and patient-centred outcomes. Emerging data confirm that the clustering of cardiometabolic risk factors is associated with steeply increased risks of sudden cardiac death, heart failure, and all-cause mortality in ageing populations, but robust intervention trials targeting these clusters in older, frail individuals are scarce. Furthermore, evidence for newer pharmacologic agents (such as SGLT2 inhibitors, GLP-1 receptor agonists, and PCSK9 inhibitors) in the oldest-old with functional impairment and polypharmacy is limited, leading to wide practice variation and frequent extrapolation from younger cohorts. summary_short: Emerging data confirm that the clustering of cardiometabolic risk factors is associated with steeply increased risks of sudden cardiac death, heart failure, and all-cause mortality in ageing populations, but robust intervention trials targeting these clusters in older, frail individuals are scarce.

title: Appraising Evidence for Hippocampal Synaptic Restoration by Traditional Chinese Medicine-Derived Antidepressant Interventions: Causality, Exposure, and Translation.
abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM)-derived interventions have been associated with antidepressant-like behavioral effects and changes in markers of hippocampal plasticity, but evidence of functional synaptic recovery remains limited. This critical narrative review evaluates 29 purposively selected preclinical reports using six qualitative appraisal domains: mechanistic causality, independent replication, anatomical resolution, methodological reporting, central target exposure, and clinical translation. The selected reports examined interventions including Yueju, Xiaoyaosan, ginsenoside Rb1, baicalin, and danshensu in stress-based models and behavioral screening paradigms. Behavioral effects and changes in AMPA receptor-associated signaling, brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and its receptor tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB), mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR), and synaptic proteins were frequently reported; however, these findings cannot substitute for direct measurements of synaptic physiology. Studies of repeated-dose Rb1 and baicalin reported hippocampal cornu ammonis area 1 (CA1) long-term potentiation (LTP). In the Rb1 study, miR-134 perturbation was tested against the LTP endpoint, whereas TrkB inhibition in the baicalin study was evaluated against behavioral outcomes in separate experiments. title: Potential Links Between Ribosome-Related Stress and Cardiac Metabolic Remodeling in Heart Failure: A Narrative Review of the Evidence and Open Hypotheses.
abstract: Heart failure (HF) is accompanied by marked cardiac metabolic remodeling and disordered energy metabolism. Previous studies have focused mainly on mitochondrial dysfunction and abnormal substrate use. The contribution of translational regulation to HF-associated metabolic remodeling remains poorly understood. Ribosomes are the core sites of protein synthesis. They also take part in cellular stress responses and metabolic homeostasis. In HF, cardiac ribosome biogenesis is stage-dependent: early pressure overload and myocardial infarction can transiently increase pre-rRNA synthesis, whereas reduced markers of rRNA synthesis have been reported mainly in advanced cardiomyopathy. Nucleolar alterations have also been observed after myocardial infarction. Oxidative stress can damage mature ribosomes in non-cardiac systems, but whether this occurs in cardiomyocytes remains unknown. Ribosome-related stress may influence translational programs through eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2 subunit alpha (eIF2α)/activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4), p53, and mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR)/AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) signaling. These pathways may be associated with impaired glucose utilization, reduced fatty acid oxidation, altered ketone-body metabolism, and branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) accumulation, although evidence strength varies among pathways. This review summarizes current evidence that links ribosome-related stress to HF-associated metabolic imbalance.

title: Renal Complement, Proteasome, and Inflammasome Alterations in Obesity-Associated NAFLD.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Obesity-associated nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (Ob-NAFLD) is associated with an increased risk of kidney injury; however, the cellular pathways contributing to renal damage remain incompletely understood. Our previous studies using the Zucker rat model demonstrated that Ob-NAFLD is associated with renal injury, inflammation, oxidative stress, apoptosis, and mitochondrial abnormalities, with only partial improvement following metformin treatment. These findings suggest that multiple interacting cellular stress pathways may contribute to the persistence of renal injury. Based on these findings, the present study examined complement-, proteasome-, and inflammasome-associated proteins as additional components of the renal pathology. Methods: Female lean and obese Zucker rats were maintained on an AIN-93G diet and assigned to four groups: Lean, Lean + metformin, Ob-NAFLD, and Ob-NAFLD + metformin. Metformin was incorporated into the diet at 1 g/kg for 10 weeks. Kidney tissues collected from these animals were analyzed via Western blotting for complement-associated proteins and fragments, constitutive and immunoproteasome components, and NLRP3 inflammasome-associated proteins. Results: Compared with lean controls, Ob-NAFLD kidneys showed significantly increased levels of the C3 processing fragments iC3b and iC3dg, C5α, and CD88/C5aR1, whereas C3α showed a nonsignificant increasing trend. title: Type 2 Diabetes Amplifies Lactate Mediation of the Association Between <i>GCKR</i> rs1260326 and Circulating N-Lactoyl Phenylalanine.
abstract: N-lactoyl phenylalanine (Lac-Phe) is a circulating metabolite linked to exercise, energy metabolism, and metabolic disease. However, the metabolic determinants of circulating Lac-Phe and the influence of type 2 diabetes (T2D) on these pathways remain incompletely understood. We investigated whether the functional GCKR variant rs1260326, a strong genetic determinant of circulating lactate, is associated with Lac-Phe and whether lactate mediates this association. Genomic and clinical data were analyzed in 11,118 Qatar Biobank participants, including 2810 with untargeted metabolomic profiles. Associations of rs1260326 T-allele dosage with Lac-Phe, lactate, phenylalanine, and clinical traits were evaluated using additive linear regression adjusted for confounders. Lactate mediation of the rs1260326-Lac-Phe association was assessed using nonparametric bootstrapping and repeated after stratification by T2D status. Each copy of the rs1260326 T allele was associated with higher circulating Lac-Phe (β = 0.103, FDR = 1.7 × 10 -4 ) and lactate (β = 0.109, FDR = 1.7 × 10 -4 ), but not with phenylalanine (FDR = 0.95). The variant was also associated with higher triglycerides and uric acid and lower glucose. Lac-Phe and lactate associations were present in both non-T2D and T2D participants, with larger effect estimates in T2D. The variant was also associated with higher triglycerides and uric acid and lower glucose.

title: Combined Ligustrazine and Sinomenine Treatment Attenuates Neuropathic Pain and Associated Emotional Disturbances with Changes in Cortical Oxylipin and Neurotransmitter Metabolism.
abstract: Background: Neuropathic pain (NP) is accompanied by emotional disturbances. Although ligustrazine (LGZ) and sinomenine (SIN) have analgesic effects, their combined effects on NP-related emotional changes and underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Purpose: To investigate the effects of LGZ + SIN on pain, emotional behaviors, and cortical metabolism in chronic constriction injury (CCI) rats. Methods: A Public Evidence-informed Prioritization-Multi-omics Discovery-Targeted Validation (PMT) framework integrated cross-disease transcriptomic analysis and gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) with behavioral assessments, plasma inflammatory measurements, cortical metabolomics, customized polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA)-oxylipin annotation, targeted profiling, and pathway-based network analysis. Results: Cross-disease analysis identified 244 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and 121 DEG-GSEA candidates; 19 showed directionally concordant, nominally significant changes in independent cohorts, mainly in NP and depression, with none validated for anxiety. LGZ + SIN increased mechanical withdrawal thresholds and improved selected emotion-related behaviors, alongside exploratory changes in peripheral inflammatory markers. title: Mitochondrial–ER contact sites in skeletal muscle: a central hub in anabolic resistance and sarcopenia
abstract: Mitochondria–endoplasmic reticulum contact sites (MERCs) are critical structural hubs that integrate cellular signaling, bioenergetics and proteostasis. In skeletal muscle, a tissue exceptionally vulnerable to age-related decline, MERCs physically and functionally link mitochondria with the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR), with mitochondria to govern excitation–contraction coupling, coordinating calcium (Ca 2+ ) homeostasis and metabolic homeostasis. While Sarcopenia (age-related muscle loss) and anabolic resistance—the blunted hypertrophic response to nutrition or contractile stimuli, have traditionally been attributed to factors such as mitochondrial dysfunction, hormonal shifts, and chronic low-grade inflammation, growing evidence positions MERCs as a spatial nexus where these pathogenic processes converge. This review examines fundamental biology of muscle MERCs, detailing their specialized molecular architecture, tethering complexes, and physiological roles in Ca 2+ dynamics, bioenergetics, and proteostasis. We then evaluate how aging perturbs MERC ultrastructure characterized by the loss of structural tethers and progressive widening of SR-mitochondrial gaps and discuss how these changes are not merely correlative but are potentially mechanistically linked to impaired anabolic signaling. title: Estimated pulse wave velocity acceleration is an algebraic function of its own inputs: incremental prognostic value of blood-based biological age beyond chronological age and blood pressure in older US and Chinese adults
abstract: Estimated pulse wave velocity (ePWV) is widely reported as a measure of vascular age, yet it is computed from chronological age and mean blood pressure (MBP); whether its age-residualized component, ePWV acceleration, carries information beyond those inputs has never been tested. Among 3972 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) participants aged 60 or older (1034 deaths, 330 cardiovascular) we asked whether ePWV acceleration is a quantity distinct from its own inputs, and compared its prognostic value with blood-based biological age, based on PhenoAge and the Klemera-Doubal method (KDM), for all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, validating the comparison in two Chinese cohorts (CHARLS, n = 7892; CLHLS, n = 560). Within each risk branch of the estimating equation, ePWV acceleration was reproduced exactly from its own inputs ( R 2 approximately 1; residual standard deviation below 1 × 10 ⁻11 m/s) and correlated 0.990 with MBP, whereas the blood-based accelerations were uncorrelated with MBP. PhenoAge acceleration (hazard ratio per standard deviation 1.82, 95% confidence interval 1.68 to 1.97) and KDM acceleration (1.64, 1.53 to 1.76) predicted mortality, were well calibrated, retained incremental discrimination once spline age and MBP were modeled (change in Harrell C + 0.036 and + 0.032), and did so under machine-learning survival models and in both Chinese cohorts. ePWV acceleration added none (− 0.0001) and was not jointly estimable with MBP. title: Clonal hematopoiesis and the risk of major age-related eye diseases
abstract: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP), an age-related hematologic condition associated with systemic inflammation, has uncertain associations with major eye diseases. We aimed to investigate the association of CHIP, including its major genetic subtypes and clone sizes, with the risk of cataract, glaucoma, age-related macular degeneration (AMD), and diabetic retinopathy (DR). UK Biobank participants enrolled during 2006–2010 were followed by linked electronic health records until March 2022. Whole-exome sequencing identified CHIP as somatic driver mutations with variant allele frequency ≥ 2%. Multivariable Cox regression was applied to assess hazard ratios (HR) with 95% confidence intervals (95%CI). The DR analysis was restricted to participants with diabetes. Of 436,469 participants (mean age, 56.4 years; 54.5% women), 14,110 (3.2%) had CHIP. During a median 14.4-year follow-up, 31,165 cataract, 12,393 glaucoma, 13,644 AMD, and 2,692 DR diagnoses occurred. CHIP was associated with cataract (HR [95%CI]: 1.08 [1.03–1.14]), AMD (HR [95%CI]: 1.12 [1.04–1.21]), and DR (HR [95%CI]: 1.48 [1.25–1.74]), but the association with glaucoma overall did not reach statistical significance (HR [95%CI]: 1.08 [0.99–1.17]). The glaucoma association was statistically significant among participants without hypertension (HR [95%CI]: 1.22 [1.06–1.40]; P for interaction = 0.012). title: Macadamia Nut Oil Alleviates Aβ-Induced Neurotoxicity and Extends Lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans by Modulating the DAF-16/SKN-1 Signaling Pathway.
abstract: Macadamia nut oil (MNO) represents a well-recognized functional lipid rich in unsaturated fatty acids, but its neuroprotective properties remain poorly elucidated. This study sought to evaluate the neuroprotective potential of MNO and explore its underlying mechanisms in an in vivo Caenorhabditis elegans model. In this study, the in vitro antioxidant capacity of MNO was determined via chemical antioxidant assays. The results indicated that MNO possessed strong scavenging activities against ABTS, DPPH, and hydroxyl radicals. Further in vivo experiments were performed using C. elegans as the model organism. MNO treatment dose-dependently delayed Aβ-mediated paralysis and ameliorated chemotaxis ability. Moreover, MNO supplementation prolonged lifespan, reduced lipofuscin deposition, and improved nematode survival under heat, oxidative, and UV stress. Biochemical tests showed that MNO decreased ROS and MDA contents and increased the activities of SOD, CAT, and GSH-Px. RT-qPCR results revealed that MNO inhibited Aβ accumulation and daf-2 expression and upregulated longevity and stress-related genes including daf-16, skn-1, sod-3, gst-4, sir-2.1, and hsp-16.2. MNO promoted nuclear translocation of DAF-16 and SKN-1 and increased downstream sod-3 and gst-4 fluorescent reporter expression; mutant assays verified that both signaling pathways are indispensable for MNO-derived protection. title: Association between addiction consult exposure and provider adoption of buprenorphine initiation.
abstract: Background and objectives Addiction consult services (ACSs) increase inpatient treatment for opioid use disorder (OUD) and may support prescribing capacity among non-specialists. We evaluated whether cumulative provider-level ACS exposure was associated with independent buprenorphine initiation. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of providers caring for hospitalized adults with OUD at an academic medical center (2018-2026). Providers entered at their first qualifying inpatient or emergency department encounter. Cumulative ACS exposure at initiation or censoring was categorized as 0, 1-2, 3-5, or ≥6 ACS-involved encounters. The outcome was time to first observed buprenorphine initiation during an encounter without an ACS consult. Sensitivity analyses examined consult-exposed providers, study-entry era, and exclusion of ED providers. Results Among 3,410 providers, 582 (17.1%) independently initiated buprenorphine. Compared with providers with no ACS exposure, providers with ≥6 exposures had a higher average rate of independent initiation (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 1.74; 95% CI, 1.40-2.16), whereas estimates for 1-2 and 3-5 exposures were not significant. Among consult-exposed providers, ≥6 versus 1-2 exposures was associated with a higher initiation rate (aHR, 1.78; 95% CI, 1.37-2.30). title: SPOP mutations impair CRL3<sup>SPOP</sup>-mediated survivin degradation to confer chemotherapy resistance in prostate cancer: implications for survivin-targeted therapy.
abstract: Dysregulated apoptosis is a critical factor contributing to the emergence of drug resistance in cancer chemotherapy. Survivin, a key member of the inhibitor of apoptosis protein (IAP) family, is frequently overexpressed in various cancers and plays a pivotal role in apoptosis regulation. In our study, we identified CRL3 SPOP as a canonical E3 ligase for survivin, mediating its ubiquitination and subsequent degradation. Intriguingly, prostate cancer-associated SPOP mutants lose the ability to bind survivin, thereby impairing its degradation which leads to diminished apoptosis, enhanced cell survival, and increased chemotherapy resistance in prostate cancer cells harboring SPOP mutations. Importantly, we demonstrated that depletion of survivin in SPOP-mutated cells significantly enhances apoptosis and restores chemosensitivity. This study provides a direct mechanism for the reduced level of apoptosis in prostate cancer with SPOP mutations, and demonstrated that survivin might be a therapeutic target for SPOP-mutated patients and provided new strategies to overcome chemotherapy resistance.

title: Mismatch Negativity and General Cognitive Ability - A Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Intelligence or general cognitive ability (GCA) is fundamental to human behavior and cognition. It impacts important life outcomes like educational success, and even health and longevity have been related to differences in GCA. Understanding the biological basis of such individual variations presents a crucial goal of neuroscience. The mismatch negativity (MMN) is an event-related brain potential that can be measured when-within a series of frequent standard stimuli, rare deviants are presented-and is suggested to reflect conscious (active) or unconscious (passive) detection processes of the brain. Importantly, variations in MMN amplitude and latency have been linked to differences in GCA. Yet findings vary considerably. This preregistered meta-analysis provides a comprehensive and structured overview of the current state of research. Following the study selection process in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines, and the rating of study design quality with the Study Design and Implementation Assessment Device for Individual Difference Research (DIAD-ID), the association between GCA and MMN amplitude and latency was examined in 645 healthy adults across 12 included studies. The estimated across-sample associations between MMN and GCA were small, but significant (MMN amplitude-GCA: r = -0.09, MMN latency-GCA: r = -0.16; p < 0.01) and moderators were identified. title: Closing the evidence gap: a life course and neurodiversity-informed participatory scoping review of healthy ageing randomised controlled trials in adults with developmental disabilities.
abstract: Adults aged 18 years and older with developmental disabilities experience disproportionate adverse health outcomes across the life course and shortened life expectancy. We conducted a participatory scoping review of randomised controlled trials of healthy ageing interventions for adults with developmental disabilities, informed by the WHO life course framework and neurodiversity principles. We searched Ovid MEDLINE and Web of Science Core Collection on June 25, 2024, and April 10, 2025, and charted study characteristics and framework alignment. We included 79 trials with 8221 participants. Although 77 (97%) of 79 studies addressed at least one functional ability, only 25 (32%) targeted life course transitions, 28 (35%) targeted multiple ecosystem levels, 22 (28%) used participatory approaches, and 20 (25%) used strengths-based approaches. Life course and neurodiversity principles were incompletely integrated into intervention research, indicating opportunities to address developmental transitions, multiple ecosystem levels, social and community participation, and strengths across the life course.

title: Electrode material degradation and protection strategies in electrochemical wastewater treatment.
abstract: Electrochemical wastewater treatment technologies have emerged as promising green alternatives for the degradation of recalcitrant organic pollutants, offering compact design, minimal chemical input, and high process controllability. However, the long-term viability of these technologies is critically constrained by electrode degradation, which diminishes catalytic activity, increases energy consumption, and may generate secondary pollution through the leaching of toxic electrode constituents. From a green chemistry perspective, electrode longevity and material sustainability are paramount for ensuring that electrochemical treatment remains environmentally benign throughout its operational lifecycle. This review systematically examines the degradation mechanisms of electrode materials in three major electrochemical technologies-electrochemical oxidation, electrocoagulation, and electro-Fenton-and evaluates green protection strategies aimed at enhancing electrode durability. We discuss sustainable substrate selection, eco-friendly coating design, intermediate layer engineering, anti-fouling surface modification, self-healing coatings, operational optimization, and electrode regeneration and recycling. A comparative assessment of electrode materials is presented, highlighting their advantages, degradation modes, typical lifespans, and green credentials. title: Multi-omics profiling reveals sex-dependent cardiac remodeling and SIRT4-associated metabolic patterns during late-life aging.
abstract: Extreme longevity is accompanied by cardiac molecular remodelling, yet the basis of sex-associated adaptation during late-life aging remains incompletely understood. Here, we performed cardiac proteomic and multi-compartment metabolomic profiling metabolomic profiling of heart tissue, serum, and urine from naturally long-lived male and female mice across late-life aging stages. Multi-omics analyses revealed pronounced sexual dimorphism during extreme cardiac aging. Proteomic and metabolic changes varied between sexes and across aging transitions, particularly in pathways related to mitochondrial metabolism, oxidative phosphorylation, lipid metabolism, and redox homeostasis. Trajectory analyses further demonstrated dynamic and non-linear aging patterns, with distinct temporal patterns observed between males and females across molecular compartments. Among the identified molecular features, SIRT4 emerged as a candidate showing a prominent age-associated change in the female cardiac proteome and associations with mitochondrial metabolic processes. In addition, SIRT4-centered metabolic networks in identified associations between SIRT4 abundance and metabolic features across cardiac and systemic compartments, with more associations observed in females than in males.
